articles.title: COP31 climate talks in Antalya end without an agreement
articles.summary:
The COP31 climate summit in Antalya ended on Sunday without a final agreement, after a draft that did not mention fossil fuels was rejected about 44 hours after the scheduled close, the ABC reported. CBS News said European countries opposed the text, arguing it placated fuel exporters, while the ABC reported Russia and Saudi Arabia supported leaving fossil fuels out.

Australia's Climate Minister Chris Bowen, who co-led the talks with Türkiye, called the result "very disappointing". Ireland's climate minister said the talks had been taken over by some oil states. The ABC said the last UN climate talks to fail to reach a consensus deal were in Copenhagen in 2009.
keyFacts: Draft rejected about 44 hours after the summit's scheduled close
EU states refused a text that left out fossil fuels
Bowen called the outcome 'very disappointing'

articles.title: Government has four sitting days left to pass key bills before parliament's summer break
articles.summary:
Federal parliament returns on Monday for its last sitting week of 2026, with the government seeking to pass bills including a digital duty of care for online platforms and gas export reservation rules, AAP reported. The Greens want platforms fined 10 per cent of global revenue for breaches, while the Coalition says it will oppose the bill, calling it censorship.

AAP said Labor needs the opposition's support for the gas rules, which would let companies set aside up to 20 per cent of exports for local use. A Newspoll published in The Australian on Monday had Opposition Leader Angus Taylor ahead of Anthony Albanese as preferred prime minister for the first time, according to AAP.
keyFacts: Four sitting days remain before the summer break
Gas rules would reserve up to 20% of exports for local use
Newspoll has Taylor ahead as preferred PM for the first time

articles.title: Zelenskyy asks US to approve Patriot missile deliveries after strike on building near Kyiv
articles.summary:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy on Sunday urged Washington to approve delivery of Patriot interceptor missiles, saying partners had already paid for them through a NATO-coordinated program, Al Jazeera reported. He said Russia fired about 2,700 attack drones, 1,460 guided bombs and 165 missiles at Ukraine over the past week.

A Russian strike early on Sunday partly collapsed a five-storey apartment building in Dymer, north of Kyiv. Rescuers recovered two bodies while searching for 11 missing people, according to Interfax citing Radio Liberty. Russia's defence ministry said it struck a cargo ship near Odesa and energy sites in Zaporizhzhia; those claims were not independently verified.
keyFacts: Zelenskyy says the missiles are paid for but await US approval
Two bodies recovered and 11 missing after Dymer strike
Russia says it hit a cargo ship near Odesa; not verified

articles.title: UKMTO reports tanker incident in Gulf of Oman; Iran says two tankers hit mines
articles.summary:
The UK Maritime Trade Operations centre said on Sunday it had received a report of an incident involving a tanker and military forces in the Gulf of Oman and that investigations were under way, ABC News (US) reported. Separately, Iran's Revolutionary Guards navy said, via state media, that two tankers on unauthorised routes struck sea mines north of Ghanem Island and stopped.

It was not confirmed whether the two reports referred to the same event. The incidents follow attacks on two tankers in the Strait of Hormuz on Saturday reported by UKMTO, according to CBS News. No casualties had been reported in the Sunday incidents.
keyFacts: UKMTO says it is investigating a tanker incident
IRGC says two tankers hit mines north of Ghanem Island
Unclear whether the reports describe the same event

articles.title: Russian vessel hit by suspected sea drone at Benghazi naval base, eastern Libya says
articles.summary:
A suspected sea drone hit a Russian vessel at a naval base in Benghazi on Sunday, causing an explosion and a brief fire, according to Libya's eastern-based government, Al Jazeera reported. Reuters reported an unspecified number of people were injured.

The eastern administration said the ship had docked to refuel and take on supplies under a cooperation agreement with Russia, and that it had opened a joint investigation with Moscow into who was responsible. It said the fire was under control, called the attack a breach of Libya's sovereignty, and said Libya was not a party to the war between Russia and Ukraine. No group had claimed responsibility.
keyFacts: Explosion and brief fire on Russian vessel at Benghazi base
Eastern Libyan government and Russia open joint investigation
No claim of responsibility reported

articles.title: Drone attacks near Khartoum kill four and damage UN building, officials say
articles.summary:
Drone attacks blamed on Sudan's Rapid Support Forces killed four people in and around Khartoum early on Sunday and damaged a United Nations building, according to local reports and UN officials cited by Al Jazeera. A drone that hit a home in northern Omdurman killed three people and wounded nine, and a child was killed south of the capital.

UN humanitarian coordinator Denise Brown said a UN building was damaged while staff were inside, and the UN's humanitarian office called the danger to staff unacceptable. A Sudanese army source told AFP the drones were launched from Ethiopia; that claim was not independently verified, and Ethiopia has denied similar accusations before.
keyFacts: Four killed in drone attacks in and around Khartoum
UN building damaged with staff inside, UN says
Army source alleges drones came from Ethiopia; unverified

articles.title: Settlers burn cars in several West Bank villages; Eisenkot and Ben-Gvir dispute blame
articles.summary:
Israeli settlers attacked several Palestinian villages in the central occupied West Bank early on Sunday, burning 12 vehicles and spray-painting slogans in Ramallah and el-Bireh areas, the Palestinian news agency Wafa reported, according to Al Jazeera. Incidents were reported in Kafr Malik, Deir Abu Mash'al and Deir al-Sudan.

Gadi Eisenkot, who has been asked to form Israel's next government, described the attacks as Jewish terrorism and blamed ministers Itamar Ben-Gvir and Bezalel Smotrich. Ben-Gvir rejected that and said Eisenkot was jumping to conclusions. The Israeli military said police and forensic investigators were being sent to collect evidence.
keyFacts: Wafa reports 12 vehicles burned in Ramallah and el-Bireh areas
Eisenkot blamed far-right ministers; Ben-Gvir rejected it
Israeli military says investigators sent to the sites

articles.title: Houthis say Sanaa fuel station strike wounded six; Saudis say they intercepted a drone
articles.summary:
Houthi-run media said an air attack on a state oil company fuel station in Sanaa on Sunday wounded six employees, and a health ministry spokesperson said Saudi aircraft carried it out, Al Jazeera reported. The Saudi-led coalition did not comment on that claim.

Coalition spokesman Turki al-Maliki said Saudi air defences destroyed a Houthi drone launched towards Riyadh, and hours earlier said a ballistic missile aimed at the western Red Sea coast region was intercepted. He reported no casualties. Saudi authorities say Houthi attacks have killed 26 people in the kingdom since September.
keyFacts: Houthi media say six wounded at a Sanaa fuel station
Coalition says it intercepted a drone and a ballistic missile
Saudi authorities say Houthi attacks have killed 26 since September

articles.title: Wong to frame AI as a national security challenge in major foreign policy speech
articles.summary:
Foreign Minister Penny Wong will deliver a foreign policy statement to parliament on Tuesday that treats artificial intelligence as a national security challenge, the ABC reported. The ABC said the speech, titled "Securing Australia's future in a changing world", effectively stands in for a foreign policy white paper, the last of which was released in 2017.

Wong will say AI makes foreign interference faster, cheaper and harder to detect, citing reported Iranian and Russian influence operations. She will also say Australia is strengthening cyber resilience and legislating mandatory AI safety standards. Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke has said data centre ownership structures are a national security concern.
keyFacts: Speech to parliament scheduled for Tuesday
ABC says it effectively replaces a foreign policy white paper
Wong to cite AI-enabled foreign interference

articles.title: Lowy index finds US lead over China in Asia at its narrowest; Australia drops to sixth
articles.summary:
The Lowy Institute's 2026 Asia Power Index found the gap between the United States and China at its narrowest, with the authors attributing a record fall in US diplomatic influence partly to the war with Iran, the ABC reported. China ranked ahead of the US on economic relationships and diplomatic influence.

The index's authors wrote that the change owed more to US missteps than to gains by Beijing, while researcher Jack Sato said the US still holds a clear overall lead. Australia slipped one place to sixth, behind Russia. India rose to third, and Indonesia recorded the region's steepest fall in diplomatic influence, according to the report.
keyFacts: US-China gap narrowest on record, Lowy says
China ahead on economic ties and diplomatic influence
Australia falls one place to sixth

articles.title: Lebanon's president demands Israeli withdrawal and criticises Iranian interference
articles.summary:
Lebanese President Joseph Aoun said on Saturday that Lebanon faces Israeli occupation and interference from influential parties in Iran's government, in a speech on the eve of the country's independence anniversary, Al Jazeera reported. He demanded Israel withdraw from all Lebanese territory, stop attacks and return captives.

Aoun also told armed groups to hand over their weapons and pledged to bring all arms under state control. Al Jazeera said a June framework agreement between Lebanon and Israel has stalled, with Hezbollah refusing to disarm and Israel continuing strikes, including in Nabatieh, Bint Jbeil and Marjayoun districts on Saturday.
keyFacts: Aoun demands Israeli withdrawal from all Lebanese territory
He accused parts of Iran's government of interference
June Lebanon-Israel framework deal has stalled

articles.title: Gas exporters split at Senate hearing on plan to reserve gas for local use
articles.summary:
Gas exporters gave differing accounts of their domestic supply records at a Senate committee hearing on the government's gas reservation bill, the ABC reported. Under the plan, exporters must supply up to 20 per cent of annual production locally, targeting 110 per cent of forecast demand.

APLNG said it had supplied more than 1,900 petajoules to the domestic market, and Santos said it supplied the equivalent of 26 per cent of its export volumes to the east coast. Shell said must-sell provisions were unnecessary. The Grattan Institute said the 110 per cent target was too high. Senator David Pocock said the bill had loopholes; Santos rejected his argument.
keyFacts: Bill would require up to 20% of production for local supply
Exporters disputed each other's domestic supply records
Pocock says bill has loopholes; Santos disagrees

articles.title: Timor-Leste says Chinese and Russian firms interested in Greater Sunrise gas project
articles.summary:
Timor-Leste's government says Russian and Chinese companies have shown interest in developing the Greater Sunrise gas field, about 500 kilometres north of Darwin, the ABC reported. Woodside sold its 33.4 per cent stake back to Timor-Leste last month, giving the government full control.

Petroleum Minister Francisco da Costa Monteiro said the field could be developed soon, and the government plans to fund it with 30 per cent equity and 70 per cent project finance. Energy analyst Saul Kavonic told the ABC the field was not commercially viable and a Russian role was unlikely. Past estimates put development costs between $US14.1 billion and $US20.5 billion.
keyFacts: Field lies about 500km north of Darwin
Woodside sold its 33.4% stake to Timor-Leste last month
Analyst says the project is not commercially viable

articles.title: Three dead and 36 missing after fire at Indonesian sweets factory
articles.summary:
A fire at the PT Fonusa Agung Mulia confectionery factory in Banten province, near Jakarta, killed at least three workers and left 36 unaccounted for, officials said on Sunday, according to the ABC and Al Jazeera. The fire started on Saturday afternoon at the plant, which makes Milkita products.

Indonesia's search and rescue agency said 15 people had been rescued, four of whom were taken to hospital. A rescue official told AP the fire was still burning in several places more than 12 hours after it began. Survivors told local media it started near a cooling unit on the third floor, and authorities said the cause was under investigation.
keyFacts: At least three killed and 36 missing, officials say
15 people rescued, four taken to hospital
Cause under investigation

articles.title: COP31 presidency releases final text for approval as talks run two days over time
articles.summary:
Organisers of the COP31 climate talks in Antalya released what they called a final deal text early on Sunday, after negotiations ran past the Friday deadline, Reuters reported via RTÉ. COP31 president Murat Kurum told a late-night plenary he believed all parties could agree on the text, and said concerns over fossil fuels and adaptation finance had been addressed.

The ABC reported the text keeps a call to electrify the global economy but does not name fossil fuels. Delegations had until 0300 GMT to object, with an approval session set for Sunday morning in Antalya. The African Group of Negotiators said it was disappointed with several outcomes, according to MyJoyOnline. Any deal needs consensus.
keyFacts: Final text released early Sunday after talks overran by two days
ABC reports the text does not name fossil fuels
Approval session set for Sunday morning, Antalya time

articles.title: Bahrain says Iranian attack caused fire at industrial site; Iran says it targeted US bases
articles.summary:
Bahrain's Defence Force said its air defences intercepted a number of Iranian aerial attacks late on Saturday, Al Jazeera reported. The Interior Ministry said one attack caused a fire and material damage at a civilian industrial facility, with no injuries.

Iran's Revolutionary Guards said they targeted US positions at the al-Riffa and Awali bases and claimed to have destroyed two US Patriot radars, according to Al Jazeera. Bahrain and the US military did not confirm that claim, Euronews reported. Euronews also said maritime agency UKMTO reported two tankers struck by projectiles while leaving the Gulf. Iran's deputy foreign minister Kazem Gharibabadi called the US blockade of Iran an act of war.
keyFacts: Bahrain says it intercepted several Iranian attacks late Saturday
Fire at a civilian industrial facility; no injuries reported
IRGC claim of destroyed Patriot radars not confirmed by Bahrain or US

articles.title: Russian cargo ship hit by drones in Gulf of Finland; Finland says Ukraine likely behind it
articles.summary:
The Russian cargo ship Sparta II caught fire after being hit by drones in international waters west of Gogland island on Saturday, Finland's Defence Forces said, according to the ABC and Reuters via SBS. The ship, bound for Kaliningrad, later drifted into Finnish waters. Its 16 crew left in lifeboats and were taken aboard a Russian vessel.

A Finnish armed forces spokesperson said Ukraine was likely responsible. Ukraine had not commented in the reports. The ABC said the ship is under US sanctions. Finland imposed temporary air and sea restrictions in the eastern Gulf of Finland, and Prime Minister Petteri Orpo said the war was spilling into neighbouring areas. Estonia sent a navy vessel to help.
keyFacts: Sparta II hit by drones west of Gogland island
All 16 crew evacuated
Finland imposed temporary air and maritime restrictions

articles.title: NATO's Rutte pledges to defend Poland; alliance council to discuss missile incident Monday
articles.summary:
NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte said in Warsaw on Saturday that the alliance would defend Poland, after Polish authorities said Russian missiles came down in the country's south-east on Friday, AFP reported via CP24. The new development is that NATO's North Atlantic Council will discuss the incident on Monday.

Rutte said NATO would establish what happened and look for any gaps in defences. Prime Minister Donald Tusk said Poland would ask NATO to strengthen detection and surveillance, and Warsaw has called the incident an intentional provocation. The Kremlin had not commented on the incident in earlier AFP reports. The US-based Institute for the Study of War said it believed Russia fired the weapons deliberately.
keyFacts: Rutte visited Warsaw on Saturday
North Atlantic Council to discuss the incident on Monday
Tusk to ask NATO for stronger detection and surveillance

articles.title: UN weapons talks agree to work on autonomous weapons rules within two years
articles.summary:
Countries at the UN Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons in Geneva agreed on Friday to 'elaborate' an instrument on lethal autonomous weapons within two years, Al Jazeera reported, citing AFP. The Globe and Mail said the target date is 2028.

Nearly 100 countries had pushed for binding rules to be adopted quickly, but the United States, Russia and Israel opposed this, and decisions require consensus, Al Jazeera reported. Swiss chair Julien Thoeni said some countries rejected the word 'negotiate'. The Stop Killer Robots coalition called the mandate watered down, and Human Rights Watch called the outcome disappointing. Supporters of the decision said it keeps talks going.
keyFacts: CCW members agreed to elaborate an instrument within two years
US, Russia and Israel opposed fast adoption of binding rules
Decisions at the CCW require consensus

articles.title: Eleven killed in violence during capture of Mexican cartel leader, officials say
articles.summary:
Mexico's Defence Ministry said at least 11 people were killed in violence surrounding the capture of alleged cartel leader Fausto Isidro Meza Flores in Sinaloa, according to Al Jazeera and The Times of Israel. The ministry said the dead were seven gunmen and four soldiers. The capture was reported earlier; the death toll is new.

Meza Flores, known as "Chapo Isidro", is on the FBI's ten most wanted list and faces charges in Mexico and the US. Mexican officials said US intelligence assisted the operation but gave few details, The Times of Israel reported.
keyFacts: At least 11 killed, according to Mexico's Defence Ministry
Ministry says seven gunmen and four soldiers died
Meza Flores is on the FBI's ten most wanted list

articles.title: Gaza authorities say nine killed in 48 hours as displaced residents protest
articles.summary:
Gaza's Health Ministry said at least nine people were killed over 48 hours, taking the death toll since the October 2025 ceasefire to 1,661, Al Jazeera reported. Displaced residents near the so-called Yellow Line protested on Saturday as Israeli air strikes continued, according to Al Jazeera's correspondent.

Gaza's housing ministry said 350,000 families are homeless. A local mayor in central Gaza said more than 500 housing units in his area had been destroyed in under a month and described it as gradual displacement. Gaza's civil defence said it had recovered 129 bodies and remains. Israel's military has said previous strikes targeted militants; it was not quoted on these figures.
keyFacts: Health Ministry: nine killed in 48 hours
Toll since October 2025 ceasefire put at 1,661
Housing ministry says 350,000 families are homeless

articles.title: Wall Street closes sharply lower as Nasdaq falls more than 5% and Nvidia drops 14%
articles.summary:
US shares fell heavily on Friday, with the Nasdaq closing down more than 5 per cent and the S&P 500 down 3.7 per cent, according to AFP via SBS News. Nvidia shares closed 14.01 per cent lower. The close confirms the S&P 500's seventh straight losing session, reported earlier as under way.

Anthropic shares, priced at US$83 in their initial public offering, closed below US$89 after trading above US$110 on Thursday, AFP reported. ABC News said the S&P 500 is now in a correction, more than 10 per cent below its 6 October record. Analysts cited by AFP pointed to doubts about returns on AI spending and a US move to restrict Chinese remote access to Nvidia chips.
keyFacts: Nasdaq closed down more than 5%, S&P 500 down 3.7%
Nvidia closed 14.01% lower
Anthropic shares closed below US$89, versus a US$83 IPO price

articles.title: Poland says Russian cruise missile landed on its territory during strikes on Ukraine
articles.summary:
A Russian Kh-101 cruise missile came down on farmland near Nowy Lipowiec in south-eastern Poland on Friday morning, Defence Minister Wladyslaw Kosiniak-Kamysz said, according to reports cited by The Daily Caller. Polish authorities said a second suspected missile and a drone also entered Polish airspace. No injuries were reported.

Prime Minister Donald Tusk said the incident was a deliberate provocation and that Warsaw was certain the weapons came from Russia, AFP reported via SBS News. NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte described it as dangerous, according to the BBC. The Kremlin had not commented, AFP said. The incident happened during a large Russian missile and drone attack on Ukraine.
keyFacts: Kh-101 missile landed near Nowy Lipowiec, officials say
Tusk called it a deliberate provocation
No injuries reported; Kremlin had not commented

articles.title: Nvidia shares fall 14% after report SEC is examining possible accounting issues
articles.summary:
Nvidia shares closed 14.01 per cent lower on Friday, AFP reported via SBS News, after Reuters reported that US Securities and Exchange Commission enforcement staff were examining potential accounting issues at the company. Reuters cited two people briefed on the matter and could not determine when the inquiry began or its scope, according to 24/7 Wall St.

The SEC declined to comment and Nvidia did not immediately respond, 24/7 Wall St reported. The Wall Street Journal had reported earlier in the week that the SEC was investigating whether Nvidia's disclosures misled investors. The company has been led by interim chief executive Colette Kress since Jensen Huang resigned on 12 November.
keyFacts: Reuters reported SEC staff examining potential accounting issues
SEC declined to comment
Nvidia closed down 14.01% on Friday

articles.title: UK and EU sign deals on youth mobility, food trade and carbon markets at Brussels summit
articles.summary:
British Prime Minister Andy Burnham and EU leaders signed agreements on youth mobility, agri-food trade and linking carbon markets at a summit in Brussels on Friday, ABC News reported. The deals still need approval from the UK and EU parliaments.

Under the youth scheme, 100,000 young people from each side could live, work or study on the other side each year, according to ABC News and Xinhua. The food deal aims to remove most routine border checks from March 2028. The UK government estimates the deals could add up to 0.5 per cent to GDP by 2040. Burnham said rejoining the EU was not off the table. Reform UK leader Nigel Farage said Burnham had no mandate for the deal.
keyFacts: 100,000 young people a year from each side under youth scheme
Food checks to be removed from March 2028
Deals still need parliamentary approval

articles.title: Taiwan's share index falls almost 18% in its worst week since 1991
articles.summary:
Taiwan's benchmark TAIEX index fell 6.23 per cent on Friday, taking its loss for the week to almost 18 per cent, its worst week since 1991, the Taipei Times reported, citing Bloomberg. The index, which is more than 70 per cent technology stocks, has fallen more than a quarter from its 6 October record.

Taiwan's Financial Supervisory Commission has tightened short-selling rules twice this month, most recently cutting the cap on intraday short-sale orders to 1 per cent of 30-day average volume, according to the report. Global funds have sold a net US$56 billion of Taiwanese shares this quarter. AFP reported that markets in Tokyo and Seoul also fell between 5 and 6.2 per cent on Friday.
keyFacts: TAIEX fell 6.23% on Friday, almost 18% for the week
Regulator tightened short-selling curbs twice this month
Index more than 25% below its October record

articles.title: French Senate gives final approval to law presuming police shootings are lawful
articles.summary:
The French Senate voted 205 to 110 on Friday to give final approval to a law presuming that police officers who use their weapons acted lawfully unless there is proof otherwise, Reuters reported. Critics have described it as a "licence to kill".

Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said the government supports the law to protect officers working in dangerous conditions, according to Reuters. Left-wing parliamentarians said they would refer it to the Constitutional Council. A UN special rapporteur wrote to French authorities warning it could fuel impunity. Rights groups, unions and some lawmakers said it would lead to more deaths, while supporters said it gives officers appropriate legal protection.
keyFacts: Senate vote 205 to 110
Left-wing MPs plan Constitutional Council challenge
UN rapporteur raised impunity concerns

articles.title: Denmark expels Russian defence attache over alleged plot to kill Ukrainian rapper
articles.summary:
Denmark is expelling Russia's defence attache, Foreign Minister Lars Lokke Rasmussen said on Friday, after the Danish intelligence service PET said it suspected Russian intelligence of planning to kill a Ukrainian rapper at a concert near Copenhagen, Al Jazeera reported, citing AFP. The attache has seven days to leave.

PET said three people were stopped in a car near the venue, where police found firearms and knives. Two people have been charged with attempted murder and assisting a foreign intelligence service. Police suspect a banned gang helped plan the alleged attack. Russia's embassy called the expulsion vengeful and said no evidence of Russian involvement had been presented.
keyFacts: Russian defence attache given seven days to leave
Two charged with attempted murder
Russia's embassy says no evidence was presented

articles.title: Saudi-led coalition says it intercepted three missiles fired at Riyadh
articles.summary:
The Saudi-led coalition backing Yemen's internationally recognised government said it intercepted three ballistic missiles aimed at Riyadh overnight, Al Jazeera reported. Emergency alerts were issued for the capital and southern Saudi Arabia.

The attack followed coalition strikes on Friday on Houthi-held sites, including Sanaa and the port of Hodeidah, and came days after Houthi missiles hit the Public Investment Fund tower, the country's tallest building, according to Al Jazeera. The Houthis have threatened Saudi Arabia's financial district and Red Sea ports including Jeddah. The Houthis had not commented on the interceptions in Al Jazeera's report, and no damage was reported.
keyFacts: Three ballistic missiles intercepted, coalition says
Emergency alerts issued for Riyadh and the south
Follows coalition strikes on Hodeidah and Sanaa

articles.title: Paris court sentences three police officers over 2020 racist assault on music producer
articles.summary:
A Paris criminal court on Friday sentenced three police officers over the 2020 assault on music producer Michel Zecler, finding racism was an aggravating factor, Al Jazeera reported, citing AFP. Each received five years, with between three and four years suspended.

Security footage recorded the assault outside Zecler's Paris studio in November 2020. The court found his account consistent and said a falsified police report damaged the officers' credibility, according to the report. The officers had said Zecler was not wearing a mask and had tried to grab a weapon. Zecler's lawyer said justice had been done. AFP noted guilty verdicts in police violence cases are rare in France.
keyFacts: Three officers each sentenced to five years, partly suspended
Court found racism an aggravating factor
Assault was filmed in November 2020

articles.title: ABC says IDF gave no evidence for claim its former Gaza freelancer was a Hamas operative
articles.summary:
The ABC says the Israel Defense Forces has not provided evidence for its claim that Roshdi Al Sarraj, a Gaza freelancer engaged by the ABC in 2023, was a Hamas operative, despite repeated requests since 3 October. Al Sarraj was killed in an Israeli air strike in October 2023.

The IDF listed him as a Hamas operative in October 2026. An initial IDF reply cited Palestinian Islamic Jihad before being edited to say Hamas, the ABC reported. The IDF says a redacted document reported by The Australian shows him as a Hamas squad deputy commander; the ABC said it could not verify it. The Committee to Protect Journalists said its investigation found no evidence he was a combatant.
keyFacts: IDF alleges Al Sarraj was a Hamas operative
ABC says requests for evidence went unanswered
CPJ found no evidence he was a combatant

articles.title: Russia launches hundreds of drones and missiles at Ukraine, killing at least 12 over a day
articles.summary:
Russia launched 404 drones and 84 cruise missiles at Ukraine overnight into Friday, along with ballistic and hypersonic missiles, the Kyiv Independent reported, citing Ukraine's Air Force. The Air Force said 462 weapons were intercepted or suppressed. Ukrainian officials said attacks over the past day killed 12 people and injured 82.

In Kyiv, Mayor Vitali Klitschko said a ballistic missile damaged the Podilskyi Bridge and two other bridges were hit, according to AP. The Energy Ministry said power plants and substations were struck. The attack came hours after Vladimir Putin said Russia would respond to Ukrainian strikes on the Kerch Bridge to Crimea.
keyFacts: 404 drones and 84 cruise missiles launched, Ukraine says
Three Kyiv bridges damaged, according to the mayor
12 killed and 82 injured across Ukraine over a day

articles.title: COP31 talks run past deadline as countries split over fossil fuel wording
articles.summary:
UN climate talks in Antalya, Turkey, went past their scheduled Friday close with no agreed text, Reuters and AFP reported. A draft released on Thursday removed references to moving away from fossil fuels and dropped a $US120 billion adaptation finance target, according to Reuters.

AFP said about a dozen countries, including France and Panama, wrote calling for a clear transition away from fossil fuels, and an EU official said the draft was not ambitious enough. Reuters reported Saudi Arabia and other producers had objected to the earlier wording. Australia's Chris Bowen, who is presiding over negotiations, said he would keep working for as long as needed.
keyFacts: Talks continued past the Friday deadline
Latest draft omits fossil fuel transition language
Draft dropped $US120 billion adaptation finance target

articles.title: S&P 500 heads for seventh straight loss as chip stocks fall sharply
articles.summary:
The S&P 500 was down 2.2 per cent in Friday afternoon trading in New York, about 10 per cent below its 6 October record and on track for a seventh straight daily fall, AP reported. The Nasdaq was down 3.6 per cent and the Dow 0.7 per cent.

AP said chipmakers led the decline, with AMD and Broadcom each down more than 10 per cent and Nvidia down about 7 per cent. Anthropic shares were down about 11 per cent but remained above the $US83 IPO price, according to AP. The 10-year US Treasury yield fell to 4.94 per cent. Reuters reported markets were pricing a December Fed rate rise as near certain.
keyFacts: S&P 500 down 2.2% in afternoon trade
Index about 10% below its October record
Nasdaq down 3.6% as chip stocks fell

articles.title: Saudi-led coalition strikes Houthi targets including Hodeidah port
articles.summary:
The Saudi-led coalition said on Friday it struck Houthi weapons and smuggling targets, including at Yemen's Red Sea port of Hodeidah, and carried out operations in Sanaa, AP reported. Al Jazeera said the coalition also cited operations in Saada and Taiz, and its correspondent in Sanaa described the strikes as the heaviest of the conflict.

The coalition said it intercepted five drones and a ballistic missile fired by the Houthis, with Riyadh among the targets, according to AP. The Houthis threatened to attack Saudi Red Sea ports including Jeddah if Hodeidah was struck, and warned airlines to avoid most Saudi airspace, Al Jazeera reported.
keyFacts: Coalition says it hit targets at Hodeidah and in Sanaa
Coalition says five drones and a missile intercepted
Houthis threaten Saudi ports including Jeddah

articles.title: Australia and China agree to hold talks on artificial intelligence
articles.summary:
Australia and China have agreed to hold talks on artificial intelligence, ABC News reported. The agreement came from a meeting in Beijing on Friday night between Prime Minister Anthony Albanese and Premier Li Qiang, which also covered trade, climate, health and tourism.

Earlier on Friday Albanese met President Xi Jinping in Shenzhen on the sidelines of APEC. Separately, Australia signed a technology declaration with the United States aimed at protecting AI supply chains from Chinese interference, according to the ABC. Albanese is due back in Australia on Saturday after 11 days overseas covering COP31, the ASEAN summit in Manila and APEC.
keyFacts: Agreement followed Albanese's meeting with Li Qiang
Australia also signed an AI supply chain declaration with the US
Albanese returns after 11 days overseas

articles.title: France seeks UN Security Council meeting after strikes damage embassies in Kyiv
articles.summary:
French Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot said France is seeking a UN Security Council meeting after Russian attacks on Kyiv killed civilians and damaged the Austrian and Dutch embassy buildings, European Pravda reported. Barrot said Russia would have to answer for the attacks.

Africanews, citing AFP and AP, said staff at both embassies were unhurt in Thursday's strikes. Dutch Foreign Minister Tom Berendsen said the Dutch embassy was hit by a projectile. EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said the EU would summon Russia's ambassador, according to European Pravda. Russia's embassy in the Netherlands had accused The Hague of taking part in the war, Africanews reported.
keyFacts: France requests a UN Security Council meeting
Austrian and Dutch embassies damaged; no staff hurt
EU to summon Russia's ambassador, Kallas says

articles.title: Trump says US firms building AI data centres overseas will face a tax
articles.summary:
US President Donald Trump said on Friday that American technology companies building AI data centres in other countries would face what he called a tremendous tax, AP reported. He gave no details and said he had not yet told his own officials about the plan.

Trump also urged communities to accept data centres and to seek concessions from developers, according to AP and Spectrum News. Spectrum said the Senate passed bipartisan permitting legislation on Thursday, which now goes to the House. AP noted data centres were a significant issue in the midterm elections. Google and Meta say they are being more open with communities, according to the reports.
keyFacts: Trump announced no details of the proposed tax
He said officials had not yet been told
Senate passed permitting bill on Thursday

articles.title: Gaza civil defence says Israeli strikes killed six people on Friday
articles.summary:
Israeli strikes killed six people in Gaza on Friday, according to Gaza's civil defence agency, AFP reported. Spokesman Mahmoud Bassal said four died in a strike south-west of Bureij refugee camp, one in a drone strike on a tent in Deir al-Balah and one north of Nuseirat.

The Israeli military told AFP it had targeted several militants. The strikes followed an Israeli tank operation in central Gaza that the army said was aimed at a tunnel. AFP's tally puts Palestinian deaths since the October 2025 ceasefire at more than 1,600. Israel's military says seven soldiers and one civilian contractor have been killed in that period.
keyFacts: Civil defence reports six killed in three locations
Israeli military says it targeted militants
AFP tally: more than 1,600 Palestinians killed since ceasefire

articles.title: Russian diesel tankers sent under US deal arrive in Brazil instead
articles.summary:
Tankers carrying Russian diesel sent under a fuel arrangement between Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin have arrived in Brazil rather than the United States, The Moscow Times and Kyiv Post reported, citing The Maritime Executive. The Moscow Times said US buyers declined the cargoes over sanctions risks.

The Leruo and Primorye anchored at Itacoatiara on the Amazon, and a third tanker, Beast, was listed as bound for Brazil, according to the reports. Kyiv Post said Trump announced the deal on 9 October, promising more than 300,000 tonnes of diesel. The US Treasury has authorised related transactions until April 2027, Kyiv Post reported.
keyFacts: Two tankers anchored at Itacoatiara, Brazil
Each vessel carries about 40,000 tonnes
US buyers declined cargoes over sanctions risks, report says

articles.title: Cyclone Akvan crosses India's Odisha coast; officials report no deaths
articles.summary:
Cyclone Akvan made landfall near Gopalpur in India's Odisha state on Friday and weakened into a deep depression by the afternoon, according to the India Meteorological Department, PTI reported. Odisha's Disaster Management Minister Suresh Pujari said no major damage or deaths had been reported.

Chief Secretary Anu Garg said about 372,000 people had been moved to shelters, according to PTI. The state deployed 423 rescue teams. Railways cancelled dozens of trains, and tourists were barred from coastal areas including Puri and Gopalpur. The IMD said rain would ease from Saturday, with an orange alert in place for 14 districts.
keyFacts: Landfall near Gopalpur completed by late morning
About 372,000 people moved to shelters
No deaths reported, state minister says

articles.title: Pakistani minister visits India for first time since 2025 conflict
articles.summary:
Pakistan's climate change minister Musadik Malik arrived in New Delhi on Friday, the first visit by a Pakistani federal minister since the two countries' four-day conflict in May 2025, Al Jazeera reported. He is attending a Shanghai Cooperation Organisation dialogue forum that Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi was due to open.

Neither government has announced a bilateral meeting, according to Al Jazeera. Pakistan's Foreign Office said its participation reflected its role as an SCO member. India's foreign ministry said its policy towards Pakistan was unchanged. India's suspension of the Indus Waters Treaty remains in place, the report said.
keyFacts: First Pakistani federal minister in India since May 2025
Visit is for an SCO forum in New Delhi
No bilateral meeting announced

articles.title: Spanish court grants bail to US activist facing extradition over alleged Hamas funding
articles.summary:
Spain's High Court granted conditional bail to American activist James "Fergie" Chambers, who left Aranjuez prison near Madrid on Friday after nearly five months in custody, Al Jazeera and Reuters reported. The United States is seeking his extradition over the alleged laundering of $US7.5 million that it says went to Tunisia and supported Hamas.

Chambers is not charged with terrorism and denies wrongdoing, according to the report. His lawyer said the US had acknowledged translation errors in an FBI affidavit, which the court said could delay a decision. Chambers has applied for asylum and cannot be extradited while that claim is pending.
keyFacts: Released on conditional bail after nearly five months
US alleges $US7.5 million was laundered
Pending asylum claim blocks extradition for now

articles.title: UN's top court rules Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya
articles.summary:
The International Court of Justice ruled on Thursday that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya in northern Rakhine state in 2017, Al Jazeera reported. Court President Yuji Iwasawa said the judges decided 9-6. Al Jazeera said it is the first time the court has held a state responsible for genocide. The court ordered Myanmar to make reparations, including help for Rohingya to return safely and voluntarily.

The Gambia, which brought the case in 2019, called it a historic day for international justice, according to Reuters reporting carried by Al Jazeera. The reports included no response from Myanmar's military government. The opposition National Unity Government said it respected the court's authority. The US said it was studying the decision.
keyFacts: Judges ruled 9-6 that Myanmar committed genocide
First ICJ finding of state responsibility for genocide
More than 730,000 Rohingya fled to Bangladesh in 2017

articles.title: Xi tells Albanese China-Australia ties have seen a 'full turnaround'
articles.summary:
Prime Minister Anthony Albanese met Chinese President Xi Jinping in Shenzhen on Friday on the sidelines of APEC, their fifth formal meeting, AAP reported. According to AAP, Xi congratulated Albanese for leading a "full turnaround" in relations. Xinhua's readout said ties were developing steadily, AFP reported.

Albanese said both countries had worked to stabilise the relationship and would not be defined by their differences, according to AFP. AAP said no agreements were reported. Albanese is due in Beijing for talks with Premier Li Qiang and a business roundtable, where Australian firms are seeking wider market access, including for beef, which faces a 55 per cent tariff above China's quota, AAP said.
keyFacts: Fifth formal meeting between Albanese and Xi
No agreements reported from the Shenzhen talks
Talks with Premier Li Qiang to follow in Beijing

articles.title: Trump says decision on new Iran strikes can wait until next year
articles.summary:
US President Donald Trump indicated he would not decide on renewed major strikes on Iran until next year, Reuters reported on Thursday (US time). He told Reuters he would discuss it after the start of the year and told Fox News, "We'll see what happens after January 1". He told Axios and Israel's Channel 12 he was not rushing.

Iran's Foreign Ministry said US claims that Iran was developing chemical and biological weapons were an attempt to justify military action, Reuters said. Gulf News, citing Axios, said options under discussion for a joint US-Israeli operation included strikes on suspected nuclear sites. A Pentagon official put the war's cost at $US48.3 billion as of 13 November.
keyFacts: Trump points to a decision after 1 January
Iran rejects US claims about weapons programs
Pentagon puts war cost at $US48.3 billion

articles.title: ASX 200 falls for seventh straight day, down about 5 per cent for the week
articles.summary:
Australian shares fell for a seventh consecutive session on Friday, with all 11 sectors lower, AAP reported. At lunchtime the S&P/ASX 200 was down 1.17 per cent at 8,625.2, according to AAP. IBTimes reported the index at 8,594.2 in the afternoon, down 1.56 per cent and about 5.4 per cent for the week. AAP said it was likely the worst week since early 2020.

Analysts cited weakness on Wall Street and in AI-related stocks, which Anthropic's share debut did not reverse, AAP said. Technology shares fell about 5 per cent and gold was near a 14-month low. Monash IVF fell more than 20 per cent after a trading update, AAP reported. The Australian dollar was near 66.5 US cents.
keyFacts: Seventh straight daily fall for the ASX 200
Weekly loss of about 5 per cent
Technology sector down about 5 per cent on Friday

articles.title: US Senate rejects resolution to end US involvement in Iran war, 51-48
articles.summary:
The US Senate on Thursday voted 51-48 against a war powers resolution that would have directed President Trump to withdraw US forces from hostilities with Iran, Reuters reported via Al Jazeera. The House passed a similar measure 220-204 in September. Republicans Susan Collins, Lisa Murkowski and Rand Paul voted in favour and Democrat John Fetterman voted against.

Democratic Senator Tim Kaine said the 3 November midterm results showed the war was unpopular. Republicans who opposed the measure restated their support for the military campaign, according to the report. Republicans control the Senate until 3 January, when the new Congress, in which Democrats won both chambers, begins, Reuters said.
keyFacts: Senate vote was 51-48 against the resolution
Three Republicans backed it; one Democrat opposed
New Congress begins on 3 January

articles.title: European leaders meet in Berlin on Ukraine after Shenzhen summit
articles.summary:
Germany, France and the UK hosted a meeting on Ukraine at the Chancellery in Berlin on Thursday, hours after the Trump-Xi-Putin meeting in Shenzhen, Al Jazeera reported. German Chancellor Friedrich Merz called the Shenzhen meeting a "photo op" and said any deal made without Europe and Ukraine would fail.

UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham said Europe was ready to enter negotiations but a Ukraine-Russia agreement must come first, according to the report. French President Emmanuel Macron called for faster delivery of air defence interceptors. US envoy Jared Kushner, who attended with Steve Witkoff, said Trump wanted to make a deal with Europe by his side. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Europe had new sanctions ready.
keyFacts: Meeting hosted by Germany, France and the UK
Merz says deals without Europe will fail
US envoys Kushner and Witkoff attended

articles.title: US approved licences for about 879,000 AI chips to China, House data shows
articles.summary:
The US Commerce Department approved exports of about 879,000 advanced Nvidia and AMD chips to Chinese companies between December 2025 and May 2026, according to licensing data released by the House Foreign Affairs Committee, Reuters reported. Approvals included 150,000 chips for Tencent and 75,000 for Alibaba. Companies had sought to ship 3.4 million chips. It is unclear how many shipments took place.

Former US official Chris McGuire said more than 30 per cent went to firms the Pentagon lists as Chinese military companies, raising questions about the security review. Nvidia said approvals carried strict conditions and limited volumes and that it has stopped shipping H200 chips to China. AMD did not respond, Reuters said.
keyFacts: About 879,000 chip export licences approved
Committee chair Brian Mast released the data
Nvidia says it has stopped H200 shipments to China

articles.title: Japan's Nikkei drops more than 4 per cent as AI share sell-off spreads
articles.summary:
Japan's Nikkei 225 fell more than 4 per cent in early trading on Friday, following overnight losses on Wall Street, Xinhua and Reuters reported. Xinhua said that at 10am Tokyo time the index was down 2,505.50 points, or 4.21 per cent, at 56,938.71, while the broader Topix was down 1.76 per cent.

Xinhua said concern about AI-related stocks continued to weigh on sentiment. Reuters reported the Nikkei down 4.28 per cent at 56,899.52 at one point, with technology stocks tracking declines in the US. On Wall Street on Thursday, Nvidia fell 3.3 per cent and AMD 7.7 per cent, according to Reuters reporting carried by Al Jazeera.
keyFacts: Nikkei down about 4.2 per cent in early trade
Topix down 1.76 per cent
Losses followed falls in US tech shares

articles.title: US appeals court lets Trump end deportation protections for Venezuelans
articles.summary:
A US appeals court has allowed the Trump administration, for now, to end Temporary Protected Status for Venezuelans, which covers about 600,000 people, Al Jazeera reported, citing Reuters and AP. The status shields holders from deportation. The decision does not end the underlying legal challenges, and the administration has also filed an emergency request with the Supreme Court.

The administration says the protection was always meant to be temporary and that conditions in Venezuela have improved since the US operation in January that removed Nicolás Maduro. Rights advocates say his government remains largely in place, according to the report. The US State Department continues to advise against travel to Venezuela.
keyFacts: About 600,000 Venezuelans hold TPS
Ruling lets the protections lapse for now
Underlying legal challenges continue

articles.title: Danish parliament approves security deal with Greenland and the US
articles.summary:
Denmark's parliament on Thursday approved a security agreement with Greenland and the United States, with all 109 members present voting in favour, Al Jazeera reported, citing AFP and Reuters. The deal, signed in New York on 22 September, supplements a 1951 accord on the US military presence and allows the US to build two military bases in Greenland.

It also bars countries outside the EU and NATO from strategic sectors and remains in force if Greenland becomes independent, according to the report. Greenland's parliament approved it earlier in November. The agreement does not need a US Senate vote and takes effect once Denmark notifies Washington by diplomatic note.
keyFacts: Passed with all 109 members present in favour
Allows the US to build two bases in Greenland
Bars non-EU, non-NATO states from strategic sectors

articles.title: South Korea's Supreme Court orders retrial of ex-PM Han over martial law
articles.summary:
South Korea's Supreme Court has overturned the 15-year prison sentence of former prime minister Han Duck-soo over his role in the 2024 martial law declaration and sent the case back to the Seoul High Court, Al Jazeera reported, citing Reuters and AP. The majority found shortcomings in the lower court's assessment of his actions.

The justices said it was difficult to establish that Han intended to undermine the constitution, according to the report. Han has denied wrongdoing apart from one perjury charge. The special prosecution team said it respected the ruling. Former president Yoon Suk Yeol was sentenced to life in February for insurrection and is appealing.
keyFacts: Han's 15-year sentence overturned
Case returned to the Seoul High Court
Prosecutors say they respect the ruling

articles.title: One Nation pledges to scrap Victoria's climate department and VNI West
articles.summary:
One Nation would abolish the climate change section of Victoria's energy and environment department if it formed government, Barnaby Joyce said while campaigning in Kerang on Friday, the ABC reported. He said a royal commission would examine renewable energy deals and refer any suspected corruption to prosecutors.

Joyce also said One Nation would seek to revoke approved permits for the VNI West transmission line and build new coal-fired power stations, according to the ABC. Energy Minister Jaclyn Symes has previously said the government could have worked more closely with affected communities on the line, the ABC said. Victorians vote on 28 November.
keyFacts: Pledge to abolish the climate change department
Royal commission into renewable energy deals proposed
Party would seek to revoke VNI West permits

articles.title: Judge lets Trump's defamation suit against NYT and Penguin Random House proceed
articles.summary:
A federal judge in Tampa, Florida, ruled on Thursday that Donald Trump's defamation lawsuit against The New York Times and Penguin Random House can go ahead, Reuters reported via Al Jazeera. Judge Steven Merryday dismissed two of Trump's claims but found the rest plausibly alleged defamation.

The suit cites statements in a book by Peter Baker and articles by Susanne Craig and Russ Buettner, which Trump says were false and aimed at harming his 2024 campaign. The Times and Penguin deny defaming him and argued that some statements were opinion and that the suit was legally flawed, according to the report. Press freedom groups have criticised Trump's lawsuits against media outlets.
keyFacts: Judge Steven Merryday allowed most claims to proceed
Two of Trump's claims were dismissed
Defendants deny defamation

articles.title: Democrats say law firm gave Trump administration $US11.8m in free legal work
articles.summary:
Democratic lawmakers Jamie Raskin, Richard Blumenthal and Adam Schiff said law firm Kirkland & Ellis has provided at least $US11.8 million in free legal services to the Trump administration, Reuters reported via Al Jazeera. They said the work went to agencies including the Commerce and Defense departments and called it evidence of coercion of major law firms.

Kirkland said in a November letter, obtained by Reuters, that its agreement with the White House had had little impact on its pro bono work. Its lawyer did not respond to Reuters. The Democrats said they had sought records from nine other firms. The three are due to lead investigations when the new Congress begins on 3 January.
keyFacts: Democrats cite at least $US11.8m in free services
Kirkland says the deal had little impact on pro bono work
Records sought from nine other firms

articles.title: Fire set at family home of Bangladesh's former interim leader Yunus
articles.summary:
The ancestral home of Muhammad Yunus, Bangladesh's former interim leader, was set on fire in Chittagong late on Wednesday, police said, according to AFP and AP reporting carried by Al Jazeera. A police patrol put out the flames, which damaged a disused ground-floor storeroom. No one was hurt and those responsible have not been identified.

The report said 22 Grameen Bank branches had been targeted by arson in recent days, during protests by supporters of former prime minister Sheikh Hasina. Hasina, sentenced to death in absentia last year, says she plans to return in December. Police said 107 people had been arrested since Wednesday.
keyFacts: Police say fire was deliberately lit
No injuries; investigation under way
107 arrests reported since Wednesday

articles.title: Hegseth visits Colombia; both sides deny report of rejected military deal
articles.summary:
US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth visited Bogota on Wednesday and said the US and Colombia were "completely on the same page", Al Jazeera reported. He met Colombian Defence Minister Jorge Mora and presented a C-130 aircraft to the air force. No new funding was announced.

The New York Times reported that President Abelardo de la Espriella rejected direct US intervention against drug traffickers and that Hegseth shortened his visit over a declined military agreement. Both Hegseth and de la Espriella said the report was false, according to Al Jazeera. De la Espriella said direct intervention would need congressional approval. Hegseth travelled on to Ecuador and Honduras.
keyFacts: Hegseth met Colombia's defence minister in Bogota
Both governments deny NYT report of a rejected deal
Colombia likely to host next year's AC3 meeting

articles.title: Four dead after migrant boat capsizes off Senegal as Canaries arrivals rise
articles.summary:
Four bodies were recovered after a migrant boat capsized near Yenne, south of Dakar, Boubacar Seye of the group Horizons Sans Frontieres told Reuters, as reported by Al Jazeera. A local official said at least 50 people were on board. Searches continued and the number missing was unclear.

Spain's Interior Ministry said 24,364 migrants reached the Canary Islands between 1 January and 15 November, up from 14,690 a year earlier, including 11,037 in the first half of November. The UN refugee agency says nearly 600 people have died this year trying to reach the islands. Senegal's President Faye has asked for an assessment of irregular migration.
keyFacts: At least 50 people were reportedly on board
Canaries arrivals up about two-thirds this year
UNHCR reports nearly 600 deaths on the route in 2026

articles.title: Six killed in suspected gas explosion at Tbilisi apartment building
articles.summary:
Six people, including a child, were killed when a suspected gas explosion partly collapsed a five-storey apartment building in Tbilisi, Georgia, on Thursday morning, AFP reported via Al Jazeera. A three-year-old girl was rescued alive after several hours.

Georgia's Interior Minister Sulkhan Tamazashvili said preliminary findings pointed to a blast on the fifth floor when a resident tried to switch on a gas heater. Supplier Tbilisi Energy said the apartment was registered as unoccupied and had used no gas for a year. Prosecutors have opened a criminal investigation into possible safety breaches, and 28 families are being moved to hotels, according to the report.
keyFacts: Six dead, including a child
Preliminary finding points to a gas heater
Criminal investigation opened into safety breaches

articles.title: Trump, Xi and Putin issue joint declaration after first three-way meeting
articles.summary:
Donald Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin met for about 90 minutes on the sidelines of APEC in Shenzhen on Thursday evening and released a joint statement, the ABC reported. According to AAP and the ABC, it commits the three to UN reform, higher oil product supply and lower nuclear risk, and says bodies such as the International Criminal Court should not abuse their jurisdiction.

The statement does not mention the wars in Ukraine or Iran, the ABC and AAP said. Trump said Ukraine was discussed. Xi described the talks as constructive, AAP reported. Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk criticised the meeting in a social media post.
keyFacts: Meeting lasted about 90 minutes in Shenzhen
Statement covers UN reform, oil supply and nuclear risk
Text does not mention Ukraine or Iran

articles.title: Putin rules out partial truce and vows response to Crimean Bridge strikes
articles.summary:
Russian President Vladimir Putin said after his talks with Donald Trump and Xi Jinping that Russia would not make agreements following Ukraine's strikes on the Crimean Bridge, according to TASS as reported by the Kyiv Post. He said Moscow's response would be more painful than the damage to the bridge, IBTimes reported.

Putin said he had asked Russia's Security Council to reconsider a possible halt to strikes on energy and maritime targets. Ukraine's defence ministry said Neptune missiles hit the bridge's rail section, the third strike in a week. Russian Deputy Prime Minister Marat Khusnullin said some sections could reopen within one to two months.
keyFacts: Bridge struck three times in a week
Putin dropped a possible energy and maritime truce
Some sections may reopen in one to two months

articles.title: Second COP31 draft drops fossil fuel transition and adaptation finance figure
articles.summary:
A revised draft of the main COP31 decision released in Antalya on Thursday no longer refers to transitioning away from fossil fuels, AAP and Climate Home News reported. The text was cut from 18 pages to nine and also removed a proposed adaptation finance figure of at least $US120 billion a year by 2035 and a reference to the Pacific Resilience Facility, AAP said.

The draft keeps targets to raise electricity to 35 per cent of final energy use by 2035 and to triple renewable capacity. Chris Bowen, the COP31 president of negotiations, said it used the strongest terms likely to win approval. Environment groups including Greenpeace and the Australian Conservation Foundation criticised the changes.
keyFacts: Draft halved from 18 to nine pages
Fossil fuel transition wording removed
35 per cent electrification target retained

articles.title: Anthropic shares open 34 per cent above IPO price in Nasdaq debut
articles.summary:
Anthropic shares opened at $US111.50 on the Nasdaq on Thursday, about 34 per cent above the $US83 IPO price, according to Forbes and AAP. AAP said the company's market value briefly reached about $US2.1 trillion. The shares later eased and were up about 19 per cent at $US98.56 in early afternoon trade, AP reported.

Anthropic sold 980 million shares, raising about $US81.3 billion, which Forbes said is the largest IPO on record. Chief executive Dario Amodei told CNBC the company hoped to become investment grade, AAP reported. One fund manager quoted by AAP said the company needed to reach profitability soon.
keyFacts: Opened at $US111.50 versus $US83 IPO price
IPO raised about $US81.3 billion
Trades under the ticker ANT

articles.title: Wall Street falls as S&P 500 heads for sixth straight loss
articles.summary:
US shares fell on Thursday despite Anthropic's debut, with the S&P 500 down 1.1 per cent in early afternoon trade after an early gain of 1.3 per cent, AP reported. The Dow Jones index was down 766 points, or 1.5 per cent, and the Nasdaq was down 1 per cent at 12.45pm New York time, AP said.

Nvidia reversed an early gain of 4.7 per cent to trade lower, and Micron and CoreWeave also turned down, according to AP. Williams-Sonoma fell 13.9 per cent. The US 10-year Treasury yield eased to 5.06 per cent. Benzinga reported the S&P 500 was on track for a sixth consecutive daily loss.
keyFacts: S&P 500 down 1.1 per cent in afternoon trade
Dow down 766 points at 12.45pm ET
10-year Treasury yield at 5.06 per cent

articles.title: Israel says it has ended tank raid in central Gaza
articles.summary:
Israel's military said on Thursday it had concluded a tank raid in central Gaza aimed at destroying a suspected Hamas tunnel, Reuters reported. Reuters described it as the most prominent ground incursion across the ceasefire's yellow line since the October 2025 truce. The military said the main Salahudeen road had reopened.

Residents told Reuters sporadic gunfire could still be heard and the road remained dangerous. The Hamas-run Gaza media office said about 6,000 people fled the area on Wednesday. Gaza health authorities say at least 1,600 Palestinians have been killed by Israeli strikes since the ceasefire, while Israel's military says five soldiers have been killed in that time.
keyFacts: Raid targeted a suspected Hamas tunnel
About 6,000 people fled, Gaza media office said
Salahudeen road reopened, military said

articles.title: Riyadh tower housing Saudi wealth fund damaged during Houthi missile attack
articles.summary:
The Public Investment Fund tower in Riyadh's King Abdullah Financial District was damaged on Thursday, Reuters reported citing three sources, according to The National. The Saudi-led coalition said it dealt with a missile threat towards Riyadh and that falling debris caused material damage. It did not say whether the missile was intercepted.

The coalition said it also destroyed a cruise missile, intercepted four ballistic missiles and destroyed a launch platform in Yemen's Saada province, The National reported. Gulf News said the building is 80 storeys tall. The extent of damage and any casualties were not immediately known.
keyFacts: Tower is in the King Abdullah Financial District
Coalition blamed falling debris for damage
Casualties not immediately known

articles.title: Pentagon official leaves Ukraine meeting after criticising Kyiv's long-range strikes
articles.summary:
US Under Secretary for Policy Elbridge Colby told a Ukraine Defence Contact Group meeting in Brussels that Ukraine's long-range strikes on Russia had little military value, then left before a classified Ukrainian briefing, the Kyiv Post reported, citing The Telegraph.

German Defence Minister Boris Pistorius reportedly called the remarks "stupid", according to the Kyiv Post and The Independent. British Defence Secretary Wes Streeting said the strikes had degraded Russia's war capacity. Britain pledged 1,000 long-range drones to Ukraine, the Kyiv Post said. The Pentagon's account of the meeting was not included in the reports.
keyFacts: Meeting was held in Brussels
Colby left before a Ukrainian briefing
Britain pledged 1,000 long-range drones

articles.title: Israeli ambassador says Israel will respond to Australia's settler sanctions
articles.summary:
Israel's ambassador to Australia, Hillel Newman, said Israel would respond to Australia's new sanctions over West Bank settlement activity, AAP reported. He described the move as megaphone diplomacy. An Israeli government spokesman said responses were being considered and would be announced at the appropriate time.

Foreign Minister Penny Wong on Wednesday sanctioned three people and four organisations, including for the first time a construction company and its owner, AAP said. Settler leader Daniela Weiss and her organisation Nachala were also listed. A DFAT spokesperson said the measures support a two-state solution.
keyFacts: Sanctions cover three people and four organisations
A construction firm was listed for the first time
Israel has not said what its response will be

articles.title: Greens accuse Victorian Labor over how-to-vote cards putting Greens first
articles.summary:
Victorian Labor volunteers handed out how-to-vote cards at early voting centres that list the Greens first and Labor second, AAP reported. In Point Cook and Tarneit, where the Greens are running open tickets, the cards leave the rest of the ballot blank. The Greens say the cards are designed to mislead voters.

Premier Ben Carroll did not directly explain the cards and told voters to put Labor first, AAP said. Point Cook MP Mathew Hilakari defended them. Transparency International Australia said Victoria has no truth-in-advertising law for campaigns. The ABC separately reported an independent's card in Prahran closely resembles the Greens design.
keyFacts: Cards authorised by Labor state secretary Steve Staikos
Issue raised in Point Cook and Tarneit
State election is on November 28

articles.title: VEC isolates about 700 early votes after unauthorised person worked at Richmond centre
articles.summary:
The Victorian Electoral Commission isolated sealed boxes holding about 700 votes after an unauthorised person gained access to the Richmond early voting centre on the first day of early voting, AAP and news.com.au's News24 reported. AAP said the person had posed as a VEC casual worker.

Electoral Commissioner Sven Bluemmel said the integrity of the vote had not been compromised, according to AAP. The VEC has not said publicly what will happen to the isolated ballots. Early voting continues ahead of the November 28 state election.
keyFacts: About 700 votes isolated in sealed boxes
Incident happened on first day of early voting
Commissioner says integrity not compromised

articles.title: Productivity Commission proposes cutting business non-financial reporting
articles.summary:
A Productivity Commission interim report requested by Treasurer Jim Chalmers recommends winding back some non-financial reporting rules for businesses, AAP reported. It says mandatory climate-risk reporting should not be extended to medium-sized companies with revenue of $50 million or more from 2027.

The report also says some emissions reporting imposes unnecessarily high costs and that employers performing well on gender equality could report less often, AAP said. Commissioner Angela Jackson said reporting adds to a large regulatory load. The commission is also considering removing six-monthly payment-time reporting for small suppliers. Its final report is due by February.
keyFacts: Interim report released on Friday
Climate reporting extension to mid-sized firms opposed
Final report due by February

articles.title: Unemployment rises to 4.9 per cent as employment falls by 43,500 in October
articles.summary:
Australia's seasonally adjusted unemployment rate rose to 4.9 per cent in October from 4.7 per cent in September, according to ABS figures reported by the ABC and SBS. Employment fell by about 43,500 and the labour force shrank by 30,400, the ABC reported. Economists had expected the rate to hold steady, SBS said.

The ABC said it is the highest rate since the pandemic. BetaShares economist David Bassanese said the result strengthened the case for the Reserve Bank to hold rates in December. Moody's analysts said most of the fall was in part-time jobs. Opposition Leader Angus Taylor said Australia was in an "economic crisis", according to the ABC.
keyFacts: Unemployment rate rose from 4.7 to 4.9 per cent
Employment fell by about 43,500 in October
Youth unemployment rose to 11.3 per cent

articles.title: Trump and Putin meet on APEC sidelines in Shenzhen; no joint statement issued
articles.summary:
US President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin met on the sidelines of the APEC summit in Shenzhen, according to the ABC and ANI. The ABC reported that Trump greeted Putin with a handshake and said the pair would meet a second time later in the day.

Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov said the leaders discussed the war in Ukraine and bilateral relations and issued no joint statement, Ukrainian outlet UA.NEWS reported. Ushakov said no major announcements were made because both sides were preparing for the three-way meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping. The US side had not released its own account in the reports reviewed.
keyFacts: First in-person talks since the 2025 Alaska summit
Kremlin says Ukraine and bilateral ties were discussed
Three-way meeting with Xi was due later on Thursday

articles.title: Anthropic prices IPO at $US83 a share, raising about $US81 billion
articles.summary:
AI company Anthropic priced its initial public offering at $US83 a share, above its expected range of $US70 to $US78, AP reported. The company said on X that the price was set and that trading on Nasdaq was expected to begin on Thursday US time under the ticker ANT.

AP said the sale of 980 million shares, up from 825 million planned, raised about $US81 billion and valued the company at about $US1.5 trillion. AP said that was more than the roughly $US75 billion raised by SpaceX in June. The company's filings describe $US6.2 billion in debt and computing commitments of about $US900 billion, according to AP.
keyFacts: What changed: priced at $US83, above the $US70-$US78 range
Share sale enlarged to 980 million shares
AP reports a valuation of about $US1.5 trillion

articles.title: Trump weighing new strikes on Iran as Israel presses for campaign, NYT reports
articles.summary:
US President Donald Trump is considering another round of major strikes on Iran but has not decided, The New York Times reported, citing US and Israeli officials, according to i24NEWS and The Times of Israel. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has urged a four- to seven-day air campaign, the reports said.

Israel's Mossad chief Roman Gofman met US officials in Washington last week with intelligence that Iran is advancing chemical and biological weapons work, according to the reports. Axios reported some US officials believe the intelligence is driven by an agenda. Trump told Fox News there was an indication Iran was looking at gas. Iran has not responded to the reports.
keyFacts: The NYT says Trump has not made a decision
Israel is reported to favour a four- to seven-day campaign
US officials are reported to be divided on the intelligence

articles.title: Crimea bridge hit again overnight as rail traffic halted
articles.summary:
The bridge linking Russia to occupied Crimea was hit again just after midnight local time on Thursday, its Moscow-installed head Sergei Aksyonov said, according to the Kyiv Independent. Russia's Transport Ministry said rail traffic was temporarily suspended after a drone attack and no one was hurt, ANI reported, citing TASS.

The strike follows a Ukrainian missile attack on Tuesday that dropped part of the bridge into the Kerch Strait. The Kyiv Independent said it could not independently verify the extent of the latest damage. Aksyonov said general traffic was paused while damage was assessed. Ukraine had not commented on the latest strike in the reports reviewed.
keyFacts: What changed: a further strike overnight on Thursday
Rail traffic suspended, according to Russia
No injuries reported by Russian officials

articles.title: Labor and Coalition block Senate inquiry into electoral funding bill
articles.summary:
Labor and the Coalition voted down independent senator David Pocock's motion to refer the government's electoral reform bill to a Senate committee, the ABC reported. The bill changes political donation and disclosure rules. South Australian Liberal senator Andrew McLachlan crossed the floor to back the referral with the Greens, One Nation and crossbench.

Senate government business manager Katy Gallagher then moved to suspend standing orders to set time limits on debate for five bills, including the electoral bill and a defence bases bill, with votes from 1pm, according to the ABC. Labor's gas reservation, trust tax and capital gains tax bills were not included.
keyFacts: Pocock's referral motion was defeated
One Liberal senator crossed the floor
Five bills listed for a guillotine

articles.title: Xi and Putin hold talks in Shenzhen before meeting Trump
articles.summary:
Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin held about two hours of talks in Shenzhen before the APEC summit, the BBC reported. Xi said the relationship was stable and the two countries would keep moving forward, according to the BBC.

Xinhua quoted Xi describing a constructive and stable strategic relationship based on respect and equality, the BBC said. Newsweek reported that Xi said the two countries must advance a multipolar world. Putin was greeted at the airport by senior official Cai Qi, while Xi personally greeted US President Donald Trump, according to Newsweek. No agreements from the talks were reported.
keyFacts: Talks lasted about two hours, the BBC said
Held before Trump's arrival in Shenzhen
No agreements announced

articles.title: Marles says government still wants Port of Darwin back as Landbridge refuses to sell
articles.summary:
Acting Prime Minister Richard Marles said the government remains committed to returning the Port of Darwin to Australian hands, but gave no timeline, the ABC and news.com.au reported. Marles said the government wanted operator Landbridge to sell its interest.

Landbridge, a Chinese-owned company that signed a 99-year, $506 million lease in 2015, said it is not a willing seller and that forced divestment would breach international law, news.com.au reported. The ABC said the company has taken international legal action, calling the move discriminatory under the Australia-China free trade agreement. Prime Minister Anthony Albanese is due to meet President Xi Jinping on Friday.
keyFacts: Lease signed in 2015 for 99 years
Landbridge says it is not a willing seller
No timeline given for the buyback

articles.title: Government sets up NDIS plan management panel to tighten oversight
articles.summary:
NDIS Minister Jenny McAllister announced a Plan Management Panel to strengthen oversight of providers who manage participants' funds and to target fraud, the ABC reported. The government expects its broader NDIS changes to save $1.4 billion over the forward estimates.

Between July and September, the National Disability Insurance Agency rejected 3,600 claims worth $5.8 million over suspected fraud, misuse or non-compliance, according to the ABC. The ABC report did not include responses from disability advocates or plan managers. Details of how providers will be selected for the panel were not given in the report.
keyFacts: Panel to oversee plan management providers
3,600 claims worth $5.8m rejected July-September
Overhaul expected to save $1.4 billion

articles.title: Bupa closed two GP clinics months after buying them, ABC reports
articles.summary:
Health insurer Bupa closed GP clinics in Belrose in Sydney and Southport on the Gold Coast shortly after buying them, and converted a Seaforth clinic into a mental health centre, the ABC reported. Bupa runs 33 medical clinics and has approval to buy 68 more from Partnered Health.

Bupa said the closures followed a review of local needs, staff were offered redeployment and a hotline was set up to transfer patients, according to the ABC. A former patient and a former receptionist said services declined after the takeover; Bupa rejected claims it neglected the Belrose clinic. RACGP president Michael Wright said practices would become more corporatised.
keyFacts: Belrose clinic closed 15 months after purchase
Bupa has approval to buy 68 Partnered Health clinics
Bupa says patients were helped to transfer

articles.title: Jess Wilson pledges gas exploration process within 60 days if elected
articles.summary:
Victorian Opposition Leader Jess Wilson said she would seek expressions of interest for gas exploration within 60 days if she became premier, the ABC reported. Wilson ruled out changing Victoria's fracking laws.

The Coalition has also promised to lift the payroll tax threshold to $1.2 million, according to the ABC. Neither major party has pledged to return land tax to 2023 levels. Victorian Electoral Commission figures show 211,461 people voted at early voting centres on Wednesday. Labor's response to the gas pledge was not included in the ABC report. Early voting for the state election began this week.
keyFacts: Expressions of interest within 60 days
Fracking laws would not change
211,461 early votes cast on Wednesday

articles.title: Family First disendorses Bendigo West candidate over online posts
articles.summary:
Family First has disendorsed its Bendigo West candidate for the Victorian election, Christos Harisopoulos, over online content the party described as unacceptable, the ABC reported. A post attributed to him made claims about land sales to China by the major parties.

Party national director Lyle Shelton said Family First is a small party with limited resources, according to the ABC. The party disendorsed him on Wednesday afternoon. The ABC said he was the latest candidate in the campaign dropped over social media posts. Harisopoulos' response was not included in the report.
keyFacts: Candidate disendorsed on Wednesday
Party cited unacceptable online content
Shelton cited limited party resources

articles.title: Medics report three killed as Israeli raid continues in central Gaza
articles.summary:
Palestinian medics said an Israeli airstrike near an Israeli ground raid in central Gaza killed one person, and two others were killed by Israeli fire in Deir al-Balah and Gaza City on Thursday, SBS reported, citing Reuters. The Israeli military said it struck a militant in Gaza City and knew of no incident in Deir al-Balah.

The military said troops were dismantling a tunnel west of the ceasefire line. Hamas said the raid and displacement violated the ceasefire. The US-backed body overseeing the truce accused both Israel and Hamas of failing to meet commitments, according to the report. Gaza health authorities say at least 1,600 people have been killed since the ceasefire.
keyFacts: What changed: medics report three deaths on Thursday
Israel says it is dismantling a tunnel
Hamas says the raid violates the ceasefire

articles.title: Third US carrier arrives in Middle East; Iran says it will not wait to be attacked
articles.summary:
The USS Theodore Roosevelt carrier strike group entered the area covered by US Central Command on Sunday, joining two other carrier groups already in the region, according to a US official cited by Al Jazeera and Gulf News. Gulf News, citing ABC News in the US, reported more than 20 Navy vessels are supporting a blockade of Iranian ports.
