The Mexican government said US intelligence assisted, without giving details, according to the ABC, citing AFP and AP. CBS News reported violence in Sinaloa after the arrest, including gunfire near a baseball game in Guasave. Meza-Flores faces charges in Mexico and the US, where a reward of up to $US5 million had been offered.
keyFacts: Mexico's defence ministry announced the capture in Sinaloa
The FBI lists Meza-Flores among its ten most wanted
CBS reported violence in Sinaloa after the arrest

articles.title: Trump says he will work with Democrats to cap credit card interest at 10%
articles.summary:
US President Donald Trump said on Saturday he would work with the incoming Democrat-controlled Congress to cap credit card interest rates at 10 per cent, telling Fox News Channel he would do it, according to AP. Senator Elizabeth Warren, expected to chair the Senate Banking Committee, has said she supports a cap.

Trump proposed the cap in January, and banks opposed it, warning that cards could be cancelled or rewards cut, AP reported. An August New York Fed survey put the median card rate at about 22.2 per cent. Consumer Financial Protection Bureau figures show about 195 million Americans held cards in 2024 and paid $US160 billion in interest.
keyFacts: Trump backed a 10% cap in a Fox News interview on Saturday
Banks have opposed the proposal, AP reported
The median US card rate is about 22.2%, New York Fed data show

articles.title: FBI national crime database suffers suspected breach, US media report
articles.summary:
The FBI's National Crime Information Center, which police use to share warrant and background-check information, has suffered a suspected breach, CNN and NBC reported on Friday, citing two people briefed on the matter, according to Al Jazeera. NBC separately reported an apparent cyberattack on the US Department of Agriculture.

President Donald Trump appeared to confirm the FBI hack in a television interview on Saturday, saying it was "not good", Al Jazeera reported. The FBI and the Agriculture Department did not immediately respond to requests for comment, and FBI Director Kash Patel has not commented publicly. The breach has not been officially confirmed by the bureau.
keyFacts: CNN and NBC reported a suspected breach of the FBI's NCIC system
Trump appeared to confirm the hack in a Saturday interview
The FBI has not officially confirmed the breach

articles.title: US judge approves Bayer's $US7.25 billion Roundup cancer settlement
articles.summary:
A St Louis judge on Friday approved a settlement under which Bayer will pay up to $US7.25 billion over as long as 21 years to resolve claims that its Roundup weedkiller caused non-Hodgkin lymphoma, AP reported. Circuit Judge Timothy Boyer described the payouts as fair and adequate in a written order.

AP said participants could receive on average between $US10,000 and $US165,000, depending on factors including exposure and illness severity. Bayer denies that Roundup causes cancer, and its chief executive Bill Anderson called the settlement a milestone. Some plaintiffs' lawyers say the payments are too small, and the approval could be appealed. The cancer link remains disputed between the WHO's cancer agency and the US EPA.
keyFacts: The settlement is worth up to $US7.25 billion over 21 years
Bayer denies Roundup causes cancer
The approval can still be appealed, AP reported

articles.title: US jury finds man guilty of starting fire that became deadly Palisades blaze
articles.summary:
A federal jury in Los Angeles on Friday found Jonathan Rinderknecht guilty of arson-related charges over the fire that grew into the January 2025 Palisades Fire, NBC Los Angeles and ABC7 reported. Prosecutors alleged he started the Lachman Fire on New Year's Day 2025, which rekindled days later in strong winds. The Palisades Fire killed 12 people and destroyed thousands of structures.

It was a retrial; the first trial ended in a mistrial in June with jurors split 10-2 in favour of acquittal. Prosecutors cited phone location data and online search records. His lawyer, Steve Haney, argued the evidence was circumstantial and that fireworks could have caused the blaze. Sentencing is set for March 2027.
keyFacts: Rinderknecht was found guilty at a retrial on Friday
His first trial ended in a 10-2 mistrial in June
Sentencing is set for 17 March 2027

articles.title: New national rules for home birth midwives take effect in January
articles.summary:
From January, every midwife attending a home birth must hold an endorsement requiring extra training and 5,000 hours of work to qualify for professional indemnity insurance, AAP reported. Secondary midwives were previously exempt, and two midwives are required at a home birth.

The federal government says the change makes home birth safer and closes insurance gaps. Midwives and mothers say it could halve the number of home births, and rallies were planned around Australia on Saturday. Senators from several parties have asked Assistant Health Minister Rebecca White to reverse the change. White said the decision was made more than 18 months ago and that public home birth services remain unchanged.
keyFacts: The rules apply to all home birth midwives from January
Opponents say home births could fall by half or more
White said public home birth services are unchanged

articles.title: US sanctions Comancheros bikie club leaders over alleged cartel links
articles.summary:
The US Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control has sanctioned the Australia-headquartered Comancheros motorcycle club and Italy's 'Ndrangheta, saying both run transnational criminal networks, AAP and 1News reported. Those named include Allan Meehan, described by AAP as the club's alleged "world president", and New Zealand chapter leaders.

OFAC alleged the Comancheros facilitated large cocaine shipments. The sanctions block US-held property and bar dealings with those listed. Australian Federal Police Assistant Commissioner Stephen Nutt said members could lose access to banking. AAP said Australia does not enforce US sanctions, but local businesses may need to consider them. OFAC worked with the AFP and New Zealand Police.
keyFacts: OFAC sanctioned the Comancheros and the 'Ndrangheta
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent approved the sanctions on 19 November, AAP said
The AFP and NZ Police assisted, according to 1News

articles.title: Victorian Labor pledges health funding as parties dispute VicHealth's future
articles.summary:
Victorian Premier Ben Carroll pledged $14.4 million so emergency patient transport staff can transfer long service leave, and said Labor would keep 132 nursing positions at Werribee Mercy Hospital, AAP reported. Carroll said the Coalition would make large cuts and One Nation wants to privatise hospitals; both parties' positions on those claims were not reported.

The parties also differ on VicHealth, which the government plans to merge into the Department of Health after a December review. Opposition Leader Jess Wilson has committed to keeping it independent, a position backed by the Public Health Association and the AMA, AAP said. One Nation's Barnaby Joyce said the party faced a difficult task. Victorians vote on 28 November.
keyFacts: Labor pledged $14.4m for patient transport staff leave
Labor plans to absorb VicHealth; Wilson pledges to keep it independent
The state election is on 28 November

articles.title: Malaysia says it will resettle 10,000 Rohingya refugees in Turkey
articles.summary:
Malaysian Deputy Prime Minister Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said on Friday that Malaysia will resettle 10,000 Rohingya refugees in Turkey through a skills training program, AAP reported. He said the government would work with Turkish authorities and the UN refugee agency and would consider the consent of those involved. Turkey's foreign ministry did not immediately respond.

The announcement came a day after the International Court of Justice ruled Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya. A Myanmar government spokeswoman called the ruling unfair and said it was a nine-to-six decision. UNHCR figures show Malaysia had about 193,000 registered refugees from Myanmar at the end of February.
keyFacts: Malaysia plans to resettle 10,000 Rohingya in Turkey
Turkey had not responded, AAP reported
Myanmar called the ICJ genocide ruling unfair

articles.title: Honda and Toyota recall 1.6 million US vehicles over Takata airbag risk
articles.summary:
Honda and Toyota are recalling about 1.6 million vehicles in the US because their Takata airbag inflators could rupture, the ABC reported, citing Reuters. Both companies said no injuries, crashes or ruptures have been linked to the recalled vehicles.

The US road safety regulator NHTSA said the companies saw early evidence of degradation risk. Honda's recall covers 810,592 older US vehicles, while Toyota's covers 790,000 vehicles worldwide, including 314,000 in the US. Inflators will be replaced. Defective Takata inflators have been linked to at least 28 US deaths since 2009. Lexus has also recalled more than 7,000 vehicles in Australia, the ABC said.
keyFacts: About 1.6 million US vehicles are being recalled
The companies said no injuries are linked to these vehicles
Lexus has recalled more than 7,000 vehicles in Australia

articles.title: Fire at Iraqi power station near Basra kills at least four
articles.summary:
A fire at the Hartha power station north of Basra killed at least four people and injured 35, according to the Iraqi News Agency, as reported by Al Jazeera on Saturday. The civil defence directorate said the blaze at the station and nearby houses had been brought under control.

Operations at the 800-megawatt plant were halted, the agency said. The cause has not been confirmed. Footage shared online showed smoke and burnt-out cars near the site, according to Al Jazeera. Iraq's electricity grid has faced long-running shortfalls, and previous substation fires have caused power cuts in the country.
keyFacts: At least four people died and 35 were injured, state media said
The 800-megawatt Hartha station was shut down
The cause of the fire has not been confirmed

articles.title: India's Congress youth wing protests at Meta offices over account restrictions
articles.summary:
The youth wing of India's opposition Congress party protested outside Meta offices in Hyderabad, Mumbai and Gurugram on Friday, according to Al Jazeera, citing Anadolu and Reuters. In Hyderabad, protesters entered the building and scuffled with police. The party alleges Meta restricted Instagram accounts of its leaders on 19 November at the request of the ruling BJP.

BJP spokesperson Pradeep Bhandari accused protesters of vandalising the Hyderabad office. A party social media official told Reuters two accounts had been restored but thousands remain restricted. Police registered a complaint against four Youth Congress leaders in Mumbai. Meta had not commented on the allegations.
keyFacts: Protests were held at Meta offices in three Indian cities
Congress alleges accounts were restricted at the BJP's request
The BJP accused protesters of vandalism

leftOut.title: Sahm rule creator says Australian recession is 'entirely possible'
leftOut.summary:
US economist Claudia Sahm, who devised a recession indicator based on rising unemployment, told the ABC it was possible Australia could cross the threshold within six to 12 months. Unemployment rose to 4.9 per cent in October, the highest since 2021.

The ABC reported a 2020 Reserve Bank research note set an Australian threshold of 0.75 percentage points, and the current reading is 0.6. Economist Saul Eslake said the rule could trigger in December if unemployment kept rising at its recent pace. The RBA says it is not forecasting a recession, and chief economist Sarah Hunter told a hearing in October indicators did not suggest one was near.
keyFacts: Unemployment rose to 4.9% in October
Current reading of 0.6 points is below the 0.75 threshold
RBA says it is not forecasting a recession

leftOut.title: Victorian Labor MPs question leadership change in final week of campaign
leftOut.summary:
Some Victorian Labor MPs are questioning whether replacing Jacinta Allan as premier was the right decision, as polling shows the party trailing before the 28 November state election, ABC analysis reported. A senior Labor figure described the campaign as a disaster, and a former minister said the same of the leadership change.

The ABC said Labor is losing votes to the Liberals, One Nation and the Greens after almost 12 years in government. It said the Coalition appears set to win with a primary vote under 40 per cent, and that Liberal leader Jess Wilson has not yet released costings, which she says are coming.
keyFacts: State election is on 28 November
Unnamed Labor figures criticise the campaign
Liberal costings not yet released

leftOut.title: Liberal preferences could decide Greens contests in inner Melbourne, ABC analysis says
leftOut.summary:
ABC elections analyst Casey Briggs wrote that Liberal how-to-vote cards could decide several inner-Melbourne contests between Labor and the Greens at Saturday's Victorian election. The Liberals have put Labor above the Greens in all Greens target seats except Brunswick and Footscray.

The Greens hold Brunswick, Melbourne and Richmond and hope to regain Prahran and win seats including Northcote, Pascoe Vale, Preston and Footscray. Briggs estimated the Liberal preference choice could move final margins by two to five points towards Labor. Most recent polls have the Greens at 14 to 15 per cent statewide.
keyFacts: Liberals preference Labor over Greens in most target seats
Greens hold Brunswick, Melbourne and Richmond
Estimated 2–5 point shift towards Labor

leftOut.title: Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Qatar and UAE condemn Iran's attack on Bahrain
leftOut.summary:
Saudi Arabia, Kuwait and Qatar condemned Iran's Saturday attack on Bahrain, ABC News (US) reported, with Qatar calling it a violation of sovereignty and Saudi Arabia holding Iran responsible. CBS News reported the United Arab Emirates also condemned the attack.

Accounts of casualties differed. ABC News (US) cited Bahrain as saying two people were injured and a fire broke out at a civilian industrial facility, while CBS said Bahrain had reported no injuries. Iran's Revolutionary Guards have said the strikes targeted US air defence sites in Bahrain.
keyFacts: Four Gulf states condemn the attack
Reports differ on whether anyone was injured
IRGC says it targeted US air defence sites

leftOut.title: Piastri finishes third behind Verstappen and Norris at Las Vegas Grand Prix
leftOut.summary:
Max Verstappen won the Las Vegas Grand Prix from pole, his 75th Formula One win, the ABC reported. Australian Oscar Piastri finished third behind McLaren teammate Lando Norris after starting 17th because of a 10-place grid penalty for a new engine component.

The ABC reported the race had 35 lead changes. New world champion Kimi Antonelli finished fourth after an energy deployment problem late in the race. Charles Leclerc dropped to 10th after a 10-second penalty for a collision with Lewis Hamilton, who finished seventh.
keyFacts: Verstappen wins from pole
Piastri third after starting 17th
Antonelli fourth after late technical problem

leftOut.title: HMAS Sydney 85th anniversary events scaled back in Carnarvon
leftOut.summary:
Commemorations in Carnarvon for the 85th anniversary of the loss of HMAS Sydney II were scaled back because the Shire of Carnarvon council has been dissolved, the Naval Association of Australia said, according to the ABC. The cruiser was sunk off the Western Australian coast in 1941 in a battle with the German raider Kormoran, with all 645 crew lost.

The association's state president, Ian Holthouse, proposed a military tourism trail linking Carnarvon and Geraldton. The shire's commissioner said the proposal had not been formally considered. About 100 people attended Carnarvon's evening service, where minister Hannah Beazley unveiled an upgraded memorial.
keyFacts: All 645 crew lost when HMAS Sydney II sank in 1941
Events reduced because the local council was dissolved
Upgraded memorial unveiled in Carnarvon

leftOut.title: Police officer shot and man found dead in linked incidents on Flinders Island
leftOut.summary:
A Tasmania Police officer was shot while on duty at Whitemark Police Station on Flinders Island at about 9.45pm on Saturday, police said, according to the ABC. Police said the officer was in a serious but stable condition, and Pulse Tasmania reported the officer was flown to Royal Hobart Hospital.

Police later found a man in his mid-20s dead in a nearby street with a gunshot wound and said they believe the incidents are linked, Pulse Tasmania reported. Police said the situation was contained. Premier Jeremy Rockliff said he had spoken with the police commissioner. A professional standards investigation is under way and police have asked for CCTV and dashcam footage.
keyFacts: Officer shot at Whitemark Police Station about 9.45pm Saturday
Man in his mid-20s found dead nearby
Police believe the two shootings are linked

leftOut.title: Man dies and two injured in three separate stabbings across Melbourne
leftOut.summary:
Victoria Police are investigating three separate stabbings in Melbourne on Saturday, the ABC reported. A 21-year-old man from Narre Warren died after an alleged stabbing on La Trobe Street in the CBD at about 8.40pm. Three people aged 17, 18 and 19 were arrested nearby and police are looking for a fourth man.

Earlier, a 24-year-old was seriously injured in what police allege was an unprovoked attack in Bourke Street Mall, and police named a man they are seeking. Police said the two CBD incidents are not believed to be linked. A 33-year-old man was allegedly stabbed in Broadmeadows; police said the people involved are believed to know each other.
keyFacts: 21-year-old man died after La Trobe Street stabbing
Three teenagers arrested over the fatal stabbing
Police say the CBD incidents are not believed to be linked

leftOut.title: Former NSW upper house MP Fred Nile dies aged 92
leftOut.summary:
Fred Nile, who served in the NSW Legislative Council for more than 40 years, has died aged 92, his family said in a statement on social media, according to the ABC. The family said he died on 21 November.

Nile led the Christian Democratic Party and lost his seat at the 2023 state election. He campaigned against abortion and same-sex marriage. Independent MP Alex Greenwich said the two disagreed often but worked together on some issues, the ABC reported. Former premiers Barry O'Farrell and Bob Carr also paid tribute.
keyFacts: Fred Nile died on 21 November aged 92
Served more than 40 years in the NSW Legislative Council
Tributes from Alex Greenwich, Barry O'Farrell and Bob Carr

leftOut.title: Wallabies beat Wales 29-26 to end four-match losing streak
leftOut.summary:
Australia beat Wales 29-26 in a Nations Championship rugby union Test in Cardiff on Saturday night local time, the ABC reported. The result ended a run of four consecutive Test losses for the Wallabies, according to the ABC's coverage of the match.

SBS News reported that centre Len Ikitau credited a renewed focus on defence for the team's performance in the second half. The Wallabies are scheduled to play Ireland next weekend, SBS News said. The win in Cardiff came on the Wallabies' end-of-year tour of Europe, with the Ireland match to follow.
keyFacts: Wallabies won 29-26 against Wales
Result ended a four-match losing streak
Australia plays Ireland next weekend

leftOut.title: Trump says he wants a 'permanent' deal stopping Iran from getting nuclear weapons
leftOut.summary:
US President Donald Trump told Fox News he intends to reach a permanent agreement that would prevent Iran from obtaining nuclear weapons, Euronews reported. He said the aim was a deal that a future president could not undo.

Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi has said diplomacy can still end the war, but that Iran's conditions include keeping its highly enriched uranium in the country, SBS News reported. Both positions have been stated in earlier reports, and no new talks were announced.
keyFacts: Trump said he wants a permanent deal on Iran's nuclear program
Araghchi says Iran still seeks diplomacy
No new negotiations announced

leftOut.title: Analysts forecast Coalition win as Victorian campaign enters final week
leftOut.summary:
Political analysts expect the Coalition to win majority government at Victoria's 28 November election, possibly on a scale similar to Jeff Kennett's 1992 victory, ABC News reported. Premier Ben Carroll and Opposition Leader Jess Wilson campaigned at early voting centres on Saturday.

A Redbridge poll for the Australian Financial Review projects a two-party preferred result of 57 per cent for the Coalition and 43 per cent for Labor, according to the ABC. Deakin University's Geoff Robinson said regional cities including Geelong, Ballarat and Bendigo were in play. Carroll declined to say whether he would hold his seat of Niddrie. These are forecasts, not results.
keyFacts: Election is on 28 November
Redbridge poll projects 57-43 to the Coalition
Analysts compare possible result with 1992

leftOut.title: Iran's Revolutionary Guards claim to have shot down US drone over Strait of Hormuz
leftOut.summary:
Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said its aerospace forces shot down a US MQ-9 drone over the Strait of Hormuz, Middle East Eye reported, citing state broadcaster IRIB. The IRGC said it was the 58th MQ-9 destroyed by Iranian forces.

The claim has not been independently confirmed. Middle East Eye's report included no US response and no details of when the incident happened or of any wreckage. Iran and the US have been at war since 28 February, and Iran has made similar claims about US drones in recent days.
keyFacts: IRGC claims MQ-9 drone shot down over Hormuz
IRGC says it is the 58th such drone
No US confirmation or response reported

leftOut.title: Araghchi says Iran still seeks diplomacy as Trump calls Tehran's terms unacceptable
leftOut.summary:
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Tehran still hopes diplomacy can end its war with the United States and that messages are being exchanged through mediators, Ariana News reported, citing Reuters and Iranian media. He said Iran wants guarantees that Washington is serious and an agreement preventing further war.

Araghchi said keeping Iran's highly enriched uranium inside the country was a red line, though a fair solution was possible. At a White House news conference on Friday, US President Donald Trump said Iran wanted a deal but not one acceptable to him. Qatari and Iranian officials met earlier in the week.
keyFacts: Araghchi says messages passing through mediators
Uranium staying in Iran is a red line, he said
Trump says Iran's terms are unacceptable

leftOut.title: Trump says Jensen Huang should get a second chance at Nvidia
leftOut.summary:
US President Donald Trump said on Friday he would like to see former Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang given a second chance, Al Jazeera reported. Huang resigned on 12 November over a scandal involving an alleged relationship with Alice Huang, a suspected Chinese intelligence asset.

Trump described Huang as a good man who had made bad decisions and said he wanted a big apology. Nvidia board chair Harvey Jones has said directors unanimously accepted the resignation and do not plan to reinstate Huang, according to Al Jazeera. Trump also said he had not lost confidence in Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick.
keyFacts: Trump backs a return for Huang
Nvidia board says it will not reinstate him
Trump says he still has confidence in Lutnick

leftOut.title: Cricket Australia board backs Pat Cummins to stay as Test captain
leftOut.summary:
Cricket Australia's board unanimously supported Pat Cummins as captain for the three-Test series against New Zealand starting in Perth on 9 December, SBS News reported, citing AP. CA said it rejected any implication that his integrity had been compromised.

Cummins has denied knowing about the use of sandpaper on the 2018 tour of South Africa. Former teammates including Usman Khawaja and David Warner have given contradicting accounts, according to the report. Cummins said he supports an independent forum on the tour and would attend. CA chair David Boon and chief executive Todd Greenberg met him in Sydney on Friday.
keyFacts: Board support was unanimous, CA says
Series against New Zealand starts 9 December
Cummins denies prior knowledge of ball tampering

leftOut.title: Man in critical condition after stabbing in Melbourne CBD
leftOut.summary:
A 24-year-old man was taken to the Royal Melbourne Hospital in a critical condition after being stabbed on Bourke Street near Elizabeth Street at about 2.30pm on Saturday, ABC News reported, citing Victoria Police.

Police said the two men were not believed to know each other. The alleged offender fled along Elizabeth Street towards Little Bourke Street, according to police, who are making inquiries. No arrest had been reported. Police asked anyone with information or footage to contact Crime Stoppers.
keyFacts: 24-year-old in critical condition
Police say the men did not know each other
No arrest reported

leftOut.title: Boy, 11, dies after being hit by ute on South Western Highway in Kirup
leftOut.summary:
An 11-year-old boy died after being hit by a ute while crossing the South Western Highway in Kirup, about 220 kilometres south of Perth, at about 5.50pm on Friday, ABC News reported, citing WA Police. He was flown to Perth Children's Hospital and later died.

The 25-year-old driver was not injured and is assisting police. A local resident told the ABC that residents had asked Main Roads to lower the town's 60km/h speed limit to 40km/h. Main Roads had been contacted for comment, the ABC said.
keyFacts: Boy hit while crossing highway on Friday evening
Driver, 25, assisting police
Residents had sought a lower speed limit

leftOut.title: Former Brazilian president Bolsonaro hospitalised with intestinal obstruction
leftOut.summary:
Former Brazilian president Jair Bolsonaro, 71, was admitted to hospital in Brasilia on Friday with abdominal pain and distension, according to a hospital statement reported by MercoPress. Reuters reported his doctor said tests showed a partial intestinal obstruction.

His son, Senator Carlos Bolsonaro, said on social media that his father was receiving pain relief and doctors were trying to treat the condition without surgery, Reuters reported. Bolsonaro is serving a 27-year sentence for plotting a coup after his 2022 election loss and is under humanitarian house arrest. He has had several operations since being stabbed in 2018.
keyFacts: Admitted to a Brasilia hospital on Friday
Doctor reports partial intestinal obstruction
Bolsonaro is under humanitarian house arrest

leftOut.title: Trump says Canada feels emboldened but he wants a fair trade deal
leftOut.summary:
US President Donald Trump said at a White House news conference on Friday that Canada was feeling emboldened but that the US was working on a fair trade deal, The Canadian Press reported. He said he had spoken with Prime Minister Mark Carney at the Asia-Pacific summit in Shenzhen.

Trump repeated claims that Canada had taken advantage of the US, according to the report. US-Canada trade talks broke down in August, and 50 per cent tariffs apply to some Canadian goods. Carney said on Wednesday a very good arrangement was possible but Canada was pursuing other trade deals.
keyFacts: Trump says he wants a fair deal with Canada
Talks broke down in August
Carney says Canada is pursuing other deals

leftOut.title: Indian minister responds to Rahul Gandhi's 'compromised PM' post
leftOut.summary:
Indian Congress leader Rahul Gandhi posted a picture of the three-way meeting between Donald Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin, writing that a "compromised PM" could never sit at that table, in remarks seen as aimed at Prime Minister Narendra Modi, The Hans India reported.

Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju said Gandhi should not make statements against India, according to the report, and the Deccan Herald reported that he questioned Congress over the 1962 war with China. BJP media convenor Ashish Usha Agarwal said a US-China-Russia meeting does not define India's global standing, citing its role in BRICS, the Quad and the G20.
keyFacts: Gandhi posted about Trump-Xi-Putin meeting
Rijiju said Gandhi should not speak against India
BJP cites India's role in BRICS, Quad and G20

leftOut.title: First Nations youth plan Canada-wide day of action against major projects bill
leftOut.summary:
First Nations youth in Canada plan a national day of action on 8 December against federal legislation to fast-track major projects, The Canadian Press reported. The date coincides with an Assembly of First Nations meeting in Ottawa.

The 243-page bill would shorten reviews and create national interest zones for pre-approval, according to the report. Organisers from Attawapiskat First Nation said it would override Indigenous rights and fail to protect the environment, and the Chiefs of Ontario support the action. Prime Minister Mark Carney has said Indigenous participation is central to his agenda.
keyFacts: Day of action set for 8 December
Bill would shorten project reviews
Chiefs of Ontario back the protest

leftOut.title: Push grows to include carbon removal in COP31 climate text
leftOut.summary:
Supporters of carbon dioxide removal pressed for it to be included in the final COP31 text in Antalya, arguing it could help reverse warming once temperatures pass 1.5C, Madhyamam reported. Carbon removal and carbon capture and storage appeared in a draft text for the first time.

The Center for International Environmental Law counted a record 700 carbon capture lobbyists at the summit, according to the report. The UN estimates 320 billion tonnes of carbon dioxide must be removed this century to return below 1.5C. Environmental groups said the focus should remain on cutting emissions rather than unproven technology.
keyFacts: Carbon removal appeared in a draft text for the first time
Record 700 carbon capture lobbyists counted
UN estimates 320 billion tonnes must be removed

leftOut.title: Kim Jong Un inspects factories after Trump leaves Asia without meeting
leftOut.summary:
North Korean state media said Kim Jong Un inspected factories producing school equipment on Friday, AFP reported via Arab News. The visit came after US President Donald Trump left Asia without meeting Kim.

Trump said he had been too busy and that he and Kim would meet at some point, according to AFP. Pyongyang has not commented on Trump's remarks. Trump has said Kim would like to meet him, which North Korea has not confirmed. The two leaders met three times during Trump's first term.
keyFacts: KCNA says Kim inspected school equipment factories
Trump left Asia without meeting Kim
Pyongyang has not responded to Trump's comments

leftOut.title: Three arrested in Senegal after newborn dies following suspected genital mutilation
leftOut.summary:
Three people, including a newborn girl's father and paternal grandmother, were arrested in Senegal's Tambacounda region after the baby died following suspected female genital mutilation, AP reported. A regional family affairs official said the procedure was allegedly carried out on 12 November, a day after the birth.

The official said the grandmother allegedly performed it without the mother's knowledge and the baby died on the way to a regional hospital. Female genital mutilation has been illegal in Senegal since 1999, with penalties of up to life imprisonment if it causes death, according to AP.
keyFacts: Father, grandmother and another woman detained
Baby died on the way to hospital
Practice illegal in Senegal since 1999

leftOut.title: Fed governor Lisa Cook refuses to attend White House hearing on her removal
leftOut.summary:
US Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook will not take part in a White House hearing on whether to remove her unless the panel and its rules change, her lawyer Abbe Lowell said in a letter, The Washington Post reported. Lowell described the process as designed to hide a decision already made.

The hearing is set for 14 December. President Donald Trump alleges Cook claimed two homes as primary residences to obtain a better mortgage rate, which Cook has called an inadvertent oversight. A three-member committee will recommend whether there is cause to remove her. White House counsel Will Scharf disputed claims the committee had prejudged the issue.
keyFacts: Hearing scheduled for 14 December
Cook's lawyer says the process is biased
Trump alleges mortgage misstatements; Cook denies wrongdoing

sources.name: The Washington Post (via The Daily Record)

leftOut.title: Man charged with terrorism offences after raids in Sydney's south-west
leftOut.summary:
A 35-year-old man was charged with making a document connected with terrorism and using a carriage service to possess violent extremist material after raids in Sydney's south-west on Friday, ABC News reported. Police allege the material related to religiously motivated extremism, including Islamic State.

The man was arrested at an Ingleburn home and refused bail, according to the ABC. A 34-year-old man arrested in Campbelltown was expected to be charged with hindering police, and a 33-year-old arrested at Wolli Creek was expected to face firearms charges. Police searched several properties and seized items.
keyFacts: 35-year-old charged and refused bail
Police allege Islamic State-related material
Two other men arrested in the raids

leftOut.title: Trump says nuclear arms limits with China and Russia will be hard to achieve
leftOut.summary:
US President Donald Trump said after talks with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin that an agreement to limit nuclear weapons would be very hard to achieve but he would keep working on it, Reuters reported. He spoke to Reuters by phone on his flight back from the three-way meeting in China.

Trump said Xi agreed with the concept, according to Reuters, while China has been reluctant to join arms control talks. Reuters cited estimates of about 410 Chinese, 3,708 US and 5,420 Russian warheads. The leaders' joint statement said a nuclear war cannot be won and committed them to dialogue on reducing nuclear risks.
keyFacts: Trump spoke to Reuters after the Shenzhen meeting
He said Xi agrees with the concept
Joint statement commits to dialogue on nuclear risks

leftOut.title: Senegal's ruling party expels President Faye and 31 other members
leftOut.summary:
Senegal's ruling Pastef party has expelled President Bassirou Diomaye Faye and 31 other members it described as inactive, Africanews reported, citing agencies. The move follows a months-long dispute between Faye and party leader Ousmane Sonko.

Faye dismissed Sonko as prime minister in May 2026, and Sonko is now speaker of the National Assembly, according to Africanews and Channel Africa. Faye launched his own party in July. Pastef holds 130 of the Assembly's 165 seats, while Faye's party holds none. Africanews said the deadlock could put IMF support and new 2027 budget spending at risk.
keyFacts: Faye and 31 others expelled from Pastef
Pastef holds 130 of 165 Assembly seats
Sonko is now National Assembly speaker

leftOut.title: Somalia orders UAE ambassador to leave within 72 hours
leftOut.summary:
Somalia's government ordered the United Arab Emirates ambassador to leave within 72 hours and recalled its own ambassador from Abu Dhabi, AP reported on Thursday. Information Minister Abdifatah Kasim Mohamud announced the decision after a Cabinet meeting.

Somalia accuses the UAE of violating its sovereignty and supporting armed forces outside federal control, according to AP. The UAE has ties with Somaliland, Puntland and Jubbaland. UAE adviser Anwar Gargash accused President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud of putting personal calculations first. The dispute follows Somalia's annulment in January of agreements with the UAE on ports and security.
keyFacts: UAE envoy given 72 hours to leave
Somalia recalls its ambassador from Abu Dhabi
Somalia accuses UAE of breaching sovereignty

leftOut.title: US House China committee urges FAA not to certify Chinese-made aircraft
leftOut.summary:
The US House Select Committee on China released a report recommending that the Federal Aviation Administration not certify Chinese-made aircraft and that the Treasury restrict outbound investment in China's aerospace sector, according to the committee. Chairman John Moolenaar said the US and its allies should tighten export controls and investment restrictions.

The report names Honeywell, GE Aerospace and Collins as having obtained licences for technology transfers involving Chinese military end users, the committee said. Reuters reported Honeywell said its projects were fully licensed by the US government. The FAA said it had not certified any Chinese aircraft, and China's embassy criticised the report.
keyFacts: Report urges FAA not to certify Chinese aircraft
Recommends limits on aerospace investment in China
Honeywell says its projects were fully licensed

sources.name: House Select Committee on the CCP

leftOut.title: US commission says China will treat Taiwan's elections as a test
leftOut.summary:
An annual report to the US Congress from the US-China Economic and Security Review Commission says Beijing will watch Taiwan's 28 November local elections and 2028 presidential vote to judge whether pressure can move Taiwan towards unification, the Taipei Times reported.

The report says China could escalate to a blockade or quarantine if its political approach fails, according to the newspaper. It lists Taiwan's vulnerabilities, including political divisions slowing defence spending and nearly $US30 billion in approved US weapons not yet delivered as of August. The report describes Taiwan as indispensable to the regional balance, the Taipei Times said.
keyFacts: Report released by the US-China commission on 19 November
Says Beijing could escalate to blockade or quarantine
Nearly $US30 billion in US arms undelivered as of August

leftOut.title: France and Germany reported to agree deal backing Spain's de Cos for ECB
leftOut.summary:
France and Germany have reportedly reached a deal that would give the European Central Bank presidency to Spain's Pablo Hernández de Cos, Eunews reported. Under the reported arrangement, Germany would take the chief economist role and France the head of market operations.

Eunews said Reuters reported Berlin would back the Spanish candidate if Markus Brunnermeier became chief economist. The deal must still be formalised, probably at a summit of EU leaders on 26 and 27 November. Each candidate needs the support of at least 16 euro area countries representing 65 per cent of the population. The Netherlands' Klaas Knot is the rival candidate.
keyFacts: Deal reportedly backs Pablo Hernández de Cos
Must be formalised by EU leaders
Dutch candidate Klaas Knot is the rival

leftOut.title: China again urges Japan to correct its statements on Taiwan
leftOut.summary:
Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun on Friday repeated Beijing's call for Japan to correct its words and actions on Taiwan, Anadolu Agency reported. He said Japan must honour four political documents between the two countries.

The day before, Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi said Japan's position was unchanged from the 1972 joint communique and called for stable ties with Beijing, according to Anadolu, citing Kyodo. She spoke before leaving the APEC summit in Shenzhen. Relations have been strained since Takaichi's November 2025 comments about a possible Japanese military response to a Chinese attack on Taiwan.
keyFacts: Beijing repeats demand on Japan's Taiwan stance
Takaichi says Japan's position is unchanged
Dispute dates from November 2025 remarks

leftOut.title: Arizona town issues business licence for planned immigration detention centre
leftOut.summary:
The town of Marana, Arizona, issued a business licence to Management & Training Corporation to run an immigration detention centre in a former state prison, AP reported, citing Arizona Luminaria. A town spokesman said there were no grounds under town code to refuse it.

Arizona Public Media said the town had twice asked the company why sexual abuse allegations were missing from a 2023 audit of the site. The company said one allegation was mistakenly omitted and the others were classed as unfounded. ICE awarded the company a $US335 million contract in September. Opponents said they would keep opposing the facility.
keyFacts: Licence dated 18 November, runs to November 2027
ICE contract worth $US335 million
Town says code gave no grounds to refuse

leftOut.title: Michigan officials estimate three in four rivers exceed E. coli limits
leftOut.summary:
An estimated 75 per cent of Michigan's rivers and streams are likely to exceed state E. coli limits, according to Molly Rippke of the state's environment department, Bridge Michigan reported. The state has tested about half of its rivers and tributaries.

The report said sources include farm manure runoff, leaking septic systems and sewage. About 12.4 million people spend time on the state's rivers each year, according to the article. Lawmakers from both parties agree the problem is serious but differ on how to address it, Bridge Michigan said.
keyFacts: About 75% of rivers likely exceed E. coli limits
State has tested about half its waterways
Sources include manure, septic systems and sewage

leftOut.title: ABC News staff reportedly placed on leave over Trump Jr business story
leftOut.summary:
ABC News reportedly placed two employees on paid leave after an internal review of an October story about Donald Trump Jr.'s business dealings, according to reports citing The Wall Street Journal and Status. An ABC spokesperson said no one's employment status had changed, Fox News and ComingSoon.net reported.

The story was removed a day after publication in October and restored with corrections, according to the reports. It had said venture firm 1789 Capital took a major stake in defence company Anduril. ABC later clarified that the firm invested $US50 million as part of a larger round. A 1789 spokesperson told Fox News the firm was considering legal action.
keyFacts: Two staff reportedly placed on paid leave
ABC says no employment status has changed
Story was corrected after publication in October

leftOut.title: Students protest across Europe over cost of living, war and education cuts
leftOut.summary:
Thousands of young people protested in cities across Europe and the UK on Friday, ABC News reported. The organising Youth Strike coalition said it planned demonstrations in about 400 cities in countries including Germany, France, Italy, Spain and the UK.

Issues raised included the cost of living, climate, education budgets, housing, defence spending and compulsory military service, according to the ABC. The Berlin rally was among the largest. In Rome a small group threw firecrackers, but events were mostly peaceful, and London police kept a rival group apart from students. Organisers said larger Paris protests were planned for the weekend.
keyFacts: Organisers planned protests in about 400 cities
Berlin rally among the largest
Mostly peaceful, according to the ABC

leftOut.title: Sydney Marathon winner Jepchirchir disqualified and banned for three years
leftOut.summary:
Kenya's Peres Jepchirchir has been disqualified from the Sydney Marathon and suspended for three years after testing positive for EPO in a sample taken before her August win, AAP reported. She has also been banned for life from the world's major marathons.

Irine Cheptai is set to be named champion, according to AAP. The Athletics Integrity Unit also announced bans for two other Kenyan runners. Race director Wayne Larden said the case showed the testing system worked. AIU head Brett Clothier said there was still a long way to go, and that Kenya's government had committed to strengthening its anti-doping agency.
keyFacts: Positive test for EPO before August race
Three-year suspension and life ban from majors
Irine Cheptai set to be elevated to winner

leftOut.title: Three 16-year-olds charged with murder over Loganholme pub shooting
leftOut.summary:
Queensland police have charged three 16-year-old boys with murder, attempted murder and arson over a drive-by shooting at a pub at Loganholme, south of Brisbane, on 24 October, AAP reported. Five people were taken into custody after search warrants were executed on Thursday.

Vana-Reese Schuster-Togiatau was shot during a boxing event and died five days later, according to AAP. Three men were also injured. Detective Inspector Ian Galpin said two people were in the car from which shots were fired, and gang involvement had not been ruled out. The three were due in Brisbane Children's Court on Friday.
keyFacts: Three teenagers charged with murder
Shooting occurred on 24 October
Police have not ruled out gang involvement

leftOut.title: Bukele expected to register for a third term as El Salvador's president
leftOut.summary:
El Salvador's President Nayib Bukele was expected to register as a candidate for a third term before Thursday's deadline, Al Jazeera reported, citing Reuters. The election is set for 28 February 2027. A 2025 constitutional change allowed a third term and extended terms from five to six years.

Rights groups say more than 1 per cent of the population has been detained under a state of emergency with limited due process, according to the report. The government says gangs have been largely dismantled. Rival candidates include Maytee Iraheta of ARENA and Rafael Aguirre of the FMLN. Registration had not been confirmed in the report.
keyFacts: Election scheduled for 28 February 2027
2025 amendment allowed a third term
Registration not yet confirmed

leftOut.title: Rohingya community in Australia reacts to ICJ genocide ruling
leftOut.summary:
Members of Australia's Rohingya community welcomed the International Court of Justice ruling that Myanmar committed genocide, AAP reported. Asma Nayim Ullah, who arrived in Australia by boat as a child, told AAP that many people's first word on hearing the news was "finally".

AAP said about 5,000 Rohingya live in Australia. Her family stayed up on Thursday night to watch the ruling from The Hague, according to the report. AAP cited estimates that about 750,000 Rohingya have fled to Bangladesh since August 2017. The article did not include a response from the Australian government.
keyFacts: About 5,000 Rohingya live in Australia
Community members watched the ruling overnight
No Australian government response reported

leftOut.title: Ministers say Treasury and RBA are not forecasting a recession
leftOut.summary:
Workplace Relations Minister Amanda Rishworth said on Friday the Reserve Bank and Treasury were not forecasting a recession and she had no reason to dispute that, the ABC reported. Health Minister Mark Butler said the coming mid-year budget update would aim to ease inflation pressure without a "slash and burn" approach.

Shadow Treasurer Tim Wilson accused the government of pursuing policies that add to inflation, and Deputy Liberal Leader Jane Hume called for action to restore business confidence, according to the ABC. The comments followed Thursday's figures showing unemployment rose to 4.9 per cent in October.
keyFacts: Rishworth says no recession is forecast
Butler rules out 'slash and burn' in MYEFO
Coalition criticises government on inflation

leftOut.title: ABC wins scoop of the year at 71st Walkley Awards
leftOut.summary:
The ABC won seven awards at the 71st Walkley Awards for journalism, held in Sydney on Thursday night across 30 categories, the ABC reported. Scoop of the Year went to an ABC Investigations team for reporting on what ASIO knew before the Bondi attack.

Other ABC winners included Foreign Correspondent's Gaza Children of War in the international category and Four Corners' Brutal Force in current affairs, according to the ABC. Walkley Foundation chief executive Shona Martyn said public interest journalism was in good hands. Other outlets' winners were not detailed in the ABC report.
keyFacts: 71st Walkley Awards held in Sydney
ABC won seven of 30 categories
Scoop of the Year for Bondi ASIO reporting

leftOut.title: Port Adelaide takes Dougie Cochrane at No.1 in AFL draft
leftOut.summary:
Port Adelaide selected Dougie Cochrane with the first pick of the AFL national draft after matching an Essendon bid, AAP reported. Essendon took Ethan Drevers at No.2 and Carlton took father-son prospect Cody Walker at No.3.

Sydney took Brisbane academy player Caylen Murray at pick nine after Brisbane fell three points short of the draft value needed to match the bid, AAP said. Nineteen players were picked on the first night at Marvel Stadium, including five Indigenous players in the first round. The draft resumes on Friday night.
keyFacts: Cochrane taken at pick one
19 players picked on opening night
Draft resumes Friday night

leftOut.title: Caitlin Foord named AFC international women's player of the year
leftOut.summary:
Matildas and Arsenal striker Caitlin Foord was named the Asian Football Confederation's international women's player of the year at a ceremony in Bangkok, AAP reported. She previously won the AFC youth award in 2011 and the women's player award in 2016.

Foord is the second Australian to win the international award, after Ellie Carpenter in 2024, AAP said. She has 152 caps and 42 goals. Iranian goalkeeper Alireza Beiranvand won the men's player award, the first goalkeeper to do so, and North Korea's Kim Kyong-yong won the women's award.
keyFacts: Awards held in Bangkok
Foord has 152 caps and 42 goals
Beiranvand first goalkeeper to win men's award

leftOut.title: Melbourne walk against family violence to begin 16 days of activism
leftOut.summary:
The 18th annual Walk Against Family Violence is scheduled in Melbourne on Friday, starting at 10am from Birrarung Marr, AAP reported. Organisers say it marks the start of 16 days of activism against gender-based violence and coincides with Transgender Day of Remembrance.

AAP spoke with survivors and advocates taking part, including a woman who now works with perpetrators of family violence. The report listed support services including 1800 RESPECT. No new government policy was announced in connection with the event.
keyFacts: 18th annual walk held in Melbourne
Marks start of 16 days of activism
Starts at Birrarung Marr at 10am

leftOut.title: Economists put recession risk higher after rise in unemployment
leftOut.summary:
Economists said the rise in unemployment to 4.9 per cent in October increased the risk of an Australian recession, AAP reported. AMP chief economist Shane Oliver put the risk at about 40 per cent and cited five Reserve Bank rate rises in 2026.

Independent economist Saul Eslake said unemployment could reach the RBA's 5 per cent forecast as early as 2027, AAP said. He said a recession indicator known as the Sahm rule could be triggered in early 2027 if unemployment keeps rising at its recent pace. October inflation figures are due on Wednesday.
keyFacts: Unemployment rose to 4.9 per cent in October
Oliver puts recession risk near 40 per cent
October inflation data due Wednesday

leftOut.title: Businesses seek wider China market access before Albanese meets Xi
leftOut.summary:
Prime Minister Anthony Albanese is due to meet Chinese President Xi Jinping in Shenzhen on Friday before travelling to Beijing for talks with Premier Li Qiang, the ABC reported. Executives from companies including BHP, Rio Tinto and ANZ are due to meet Chinese counterparts in Beijing.

The Business Council of Australia is seeking greater access for beef, rice, medical technology, resources and agricultural technology, according to the ABC. Business Council president Geoff Culbert is expected to say business confidence depends on trust and predictability. No outcomes from the meeting have been announced.
keyFacts: Albanese due to meet Xi on Friday
Talks with Li Qiang to follow in Beijing
Business Council seeks wider market access

leftOut.title: Elton John urges government to protect Australian artists from AI
leftOut.summary:
Singer Elton John used a recorded address to the ARIA Awards to urge the federal government to protect Australian artists and their work from artificial intelligence, the ABC reported. The government is consulting on changes to copyright law.

Acting Prime Minister Richard Marles told News24 he understood the concern and that creative workers should be fully compensated, according to the ABC. The government has not announced the outcome of its copyright consultation. The ACTU separately welcomed recently announced mandatory AI guardrails, the ABC reported.
keyFacts: Message delivered at the ARIA Awards
Government is consulting on copyright changes
Marles said creators should be compensated

leftOut.title: Ukrainian drones reported to hit oil pumping station in Tatarstan
leftOut.summary:
Ukrainian drones struck the Kaleykino oil pumping station near Almetyevsk in Russia's Tatarstan republic overnight, the Kyiv Independent reported, citing a Ukrainian monitoring channel and eyewitness accounts of a fire. Neither Russian nor Ukrainian officials had confirmed the strike in the report.

The Kyiv Independent also cited Reuters reporting that Ukrainian attacks over 20 days had disrupted or halted operations at 15 of Russia's 35 major refineries, according to two industry sources. Ukraine's General Staff confirmed separate strikes on two refineries in Krasnodar Krai earlier in the week.
keyFacts: Strike reported by a Telegram monitoring channel
Not confirmed by officials on either side
Site is about 380km north of Kazakhstan

leftOut.title: Marles defends Albanese's appearance in APEC photo with Putin
leftOut.summary:
Acting Prime Minister Richard Marles said Prime Minister Anthony Albanese's appearance in the APEC leaders' photo with Russian President Vladimir Putin was part of respecting the host, the ABC and SBS reported. Marles said Australia's position on Ukraine could not be clearer.

Albanese said he would respect the wishes of the host and make Australia's position on Ukraine clear, according to SBS. Greens leader David Shoebridge called for tougher sanctions on Russia and an end to Russian oil imports, the ABC reported. Criticism of the photo was reported on Wednesday.
keyFacts: Photo taken at a leaders' banquet in Shenzhen
Marles said it reflected respect for the host
Greens called for tougher Russia sanctions

leftOut.title: Marles restates plan to keep four defence heritage sites in public hands
leftOut.summary:
Defence Minister Richard Marles said four of the 67 defence sites earmarked for sale, including Victoria Barracks in Sydney and Melbourne, Fort Queenscliff and RAAF Williams Point Cook, would be retained and moved to the finance department, the ABC reported. Marles said the government could not afford to maintain unused bases.

The decision to keep the four sites was announced by Prime Minister Anthony Albanese on 8 November, Defence Connect reported. Opposition Leader Angus Taylor said the Coalition had forced the change and would keep campaigning to save other sites.
keyFacts: Four of 67 sites will be retained
Sites move from Defence to Finance
Decision first announced on 8 November

leftOut.title: Independent MP Helen Haines discharged from hospital after Wangaratta attack
leftOut.summary:
Independent federal MP Helen Haines has been discharged from The Alfred hospital in Melbourne, ABC News reported on Monday. Dr Haines lost both legs after being struck by a car outside her Wangaratta electorate office on 19 October.

Politicians from across parliament welcomed the news, according to the ABC's live coverage. A 43-year-old man, Brendan Nugent, has been charged over the incident, the ABC reported. The charges have not been tested in court. Details of Dr Haines's return to parliamentary duties were not reported in the coverage reviewed.
keyFacts: Helen Haines discharged from The Alfred hospital
She lost both legs after being hit by a car on 19 October
A 43-year-old man has been charged

leftOut.title: Estonia to close Russian border crossings after alleged GRU-linked arson attempt
leftOut.summary:
Estonia will close its border crossings with Russia from 1 December after an attempted arson attack on drone maker Threod Systems near Tallinn, The Irish Times and Defense News reported. Eight people were detained; officials said the suspects were Latvian citizens.

The head of Estonia's security police, Margo Palloson, said the attack was carried out at the behest of Russian military intelligence. The company said production was not disrupted. Russian foreign ministry spokeswoman Maria Zakharova called the accusations part of a wave of Russophobia. Estonian authorities did not say how long the closure would last.
keyFacts: Crossings to close from 1 December
Eight detained over attempted attack on Threod Systems
Russia rejects the accusations

leftOut.title: Ecuador's president denies the US has a military base at Taura airbase
leftOut.summary:
Ecuadorian President Daniel Noboa said US personnel at the Taura air base near Guayaquil were there only for temporary activities under bilateral cooperation, and that it was an Ecuadorian base, AFP reported. He was responding to an AFP investigation.

AFP reported about 20 US military flights at the base between June and mid-October, along with tents and construction work. Ecuadorian voters rejected allowing foreign military bases in a November 2025 referendum. The Pentagon, US Southern Command and Ecuador's air force did not respond to requests for comment, according to Al Jazeera.
keyFacts: Noboa says US activities at Taura are temporary
AFP counted about 20 US military flights since June
Voters rejected foreign bases in a 2025 referendum

leftOut.title: Iranian embassy posts threat naming two US Navy officers
leftOut.summary:
Iran's embassy in South Africa posted a message on X saying 'we will find you' alongside images of the commanding officer and executive officer of the destroyer USS Spruance, Fox News and The Express reported. The ship returned to San Diego after a 357-day deployment that included combat against Iranian forces.

An earlier embassy post had accused the officers of ordering missile strikes that it said killed children at a school in Minab, a claim not independently established. A Foundation for Defense of Democracies analyst said the threat should concern US officials. The US Navy's response was not reported.
keyFacts: Embassy post names USS Spruance's two senior officers
Ship returned after a 357-day deployment
Iran links the officers to a strike on a Minab school

leftOut.title: Trump calls ABC reporter 'pathetic' over question on White House renovation spending
leftOut.summary:
US President Donald Trump called ABC News reporter Rachel Scott 'pathetic' after she asked about spending on renovations in Washington while the air traffic control system needed funding, The Independent reported. Mr Trump said the White House renovations cost 'peanuts'.

The Independent cited Justice Department filings showing the ballroom cost estimate had risen from $US200 million to as much as $US600 million. Mr Trump has blamed ageing equipment and the Biden administration for Friday's nationwide flight ground stop. The Independent said total renovation projects across the capital exceed $US1.65 billion in public money.
keyFacts: Trump says renovation costs are 'peanuts'
Ballroom estimate has risen to as much as $US600 million
Exchange followed Friday's FAA ground stop

leftOut.title: Trump administration presses Congress for $US50 billion to overhaul air traffic control
leftOut.summary:
The Trump administration is seeking $US50 billion to overhaul the US air traffic control system, AP reported. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said he would send a detailed request to legislators on Monday, but had not specified how the money would be spent.

Congress approved $US12.5 billion in 2025, and the FAA administrator has said at least another $US10 billion is needed for a second phase, according to AP. The FAA has said Friday's nationwide ground stop was caused by a router overload during contractor work. Democrats are seeking answers about earlier spending.
keyFacts: Administration seeks $US50 billion
Congress approved $US12.5 billion in 2025
FAA blames router overload for Friday's ground stop

leftOut.title: Darwin girl, 15, granted bail on terrorism document charge
leftOut.summary:
A 15-year-old Darwin girl charged with collecting or making documents likely to facilitate terrorist acts was granted bail in the Northern Territory Youth Justice Court on Monday, AAP reported. She was arrested on 3 November and cannot be identified.

Judge Greg Macdonald found exceptional circumstances, citing her age, mental health and family support, according to AAP. Conditions include no internet-capable devices, adult supervision and the removal of guns from the home. Allegations raised at the hearing have not been tested. A 14-year-old boy faces related charges, and the case returns to court on 15 December.
keyFacts: Charge carries a maximum of 15 years
Bail granted with strict conditions
Case returns to court on 15 December

leftOut.title: Elderly driver who killed boy in Canberra car park avoids jail
leftOut.summary:
An 81-year-old woman who pleaded guilty to culpable driving causing the death of a four-year-old boy in a Canberra shopping centre car park received a suspended sentence of two years and three months, ABC News reported. Her licence was suspended indefinitely.

ACT Supreme Court Justice Belinda Baker said the woman was not intoxicated or speeding and did not realise the car was still in drive. Prosecutors had argued for full-time custody. The boy's parents had asked for the lightest possible sentence and said afterwards the result was fair, according to the ABC.
keyFacts: Suspended sentence of two years and three months
Licence suspended indefinitely
Prosecutors had sought full-time custody

leftOut.title: Robert Irwin named Queensland's 2027 Australian of the Year
leftOut.summary:
Conservationist Robert Irwin, 22, has been named Queensland's 2027 Australian of the Year for his environmental advocacy and work at Australia Zoo, ABC News reported. Sprinter Gout Gout, 18, was named Young Australian of the Year for Queensland.

Disability advocate Carmel Crouch, 80, was named the state's Senior Australian of the Year, and Cairns Hospital greeter Noel Brown received the Local Hero award, according to the ABC. National Australia Day Council chief executive Carrie Leeson congratulated the recipients.
keyFacts: Robert Irwin named Queensland Australian of the Year
Gout Gout named Young Australian of the Year for Queensland
Carmel Crouch named Senior Australian of the Year for Queensland

leftOut.title: Albanese says he will raise Iran war concerns at Quad meeting with Trump
leftOut.summary:
Anthony Albanese said he would raise Australia's concerns about the Iran war when he meets Donald Trump and the leaders of India and Japan in Manila on Tuesday evening, AAP reported. It is the first Quad leaders' meeting since 2024.

Protests led by left-wing groups, students and workers have been held in Manila for four days against Trump's attendance, according to AAP. Albanese said he had a good relationship with Trump and that Australia wanted de-escalation. The meeting had not taken place at the time of this update.
keyFacts: Quad leaders due to meet in Manila on Tuesday evening
First Quad leaders' meeting since 2024
Protests in Manila against Trump's attendance

leftOut.title: Zelenskiy says Ukraine, US and European officials agreed to meet in Berlin
leftOut.summary:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said Monday's online talks with US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner and European officials were difficult, and that participants agreed to meet in Berlin with the coalition of countries backing Ukraine, Al Jazeera and Reuters reported.

Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov said Russia had not agreed to widen talks beyond existing delegations and no date was set for a next round, according to the report. Kushner said Washington was making progress. Kyiv's mayor said preliminary reports indicated two bridges over the Dnipro were hit.
keyFacts: Online talks held on Monday with US envoys
Participants agreed to meet in Berlin, Zelenskiy said
Kremlin says no date set for next round

leftOut.title: CNN reports US intelligence suggests Iran drew up options for attack in Washington
leftOut.summary:
CNN reported, citing multiple US officials, that new US intelligence suggests Iran has drawn up plans that could target senior Trump administration figures in Washington with a radiological or chemical device, according to the Times of Israel.

The sources said the intelligence does not point to an imminent attack and describes options rather than operations, the report said. One source doubted Iran had the personnel to carry them out, and officials were divided on the intelligence's credibility. Iran has not responded in the reports, and the claims are attributed to anonymous officials.
keyFacts: Report cites anonymous US officials
Intelligence does not indicate imminent attack, sources say
Officials divided on credibility

leftOut.title: Victorian party leaders to take part in single town hall debate before election
leftOut.summary:
The leaders of Victoria's four major parties will take part in a town hall-style debate on Tuesday, the only pre-election debate the two major parties agreed to, AAP reported. Victorians vote on 28 November, and there will be no one-on-one debate between Premier Ben Carroll and Opposition Leader Jess Wilson.

Wilson accused Carroll of avoiding a head-to-head, while Carroll said Wilson did not want to share a stage with One Nation, according to AAP. A Monash University political scientist told AAP a debate gaffe would be high risk for the major leaders.
keyFacts: Four-leader town hall debate set for Tuesday
Victorian election is on 28 November
No head-to-head between Carroll and Wilson

leftOut.title: Robert Pattinson announced as the next James Bond
leftOut.summary:
Robert Pattinson, 40, has been announced as the next actor to play James Bond, replacing Daniel Craig, AAP reported. The announcement was made on the official 007 Instagram account, and Pattinson becomes the seventh actor in the role.

Denis Villeneuve will direct the untitled film from a script by Steven Knight, according to AAP. Production is expected in 2027 with release in 2028. It is the first Bond film since Amazon took creative control of the franchise.
keyFacts: Pattinson is the seventh actor to play Bond
Denis Villeneuve to direct
Release expected in 2028

leftOut.title: UK minister criticises Russell Brand's statement from prison
leftOut.summary:
Senior UK minister Ed Miliband described a message Russell Brand issued from prison as disgusting, AAP reported. Brand's wife read the statement, in which he said he was not guilty. He was jailed for 10.5 years for raping one woman and sexually assaulting three others.

AAP reported Brand has been moved from HMP Wandsworth to HMP Littlehey, a category C prison. Miliband also said it was time to debate age of consent laws and that he regretted a 2015 interview on Brand's show, according to AAP.
keyFacts: Brand's wife read his statement from prison
Brand was jailed for 10.5 years
Brand moved to a category C prison, AAP reports

leftOut.title: Mother denies starting fatal Russell Island house fire at coronial inquest
leftOut.summary:
Samantha Stephenson denied starting the August 2023 house fire on Russell Island, south-east of Brisbane, which killed her partner and five children aged three to 11, AAP reported. She was the first witness at a Queensland coronial inquest that began on Monday.

Counsel assisting said the fire likely started on the ground floor and deliberate ignition could not be ruled out, according to AAP. The inquest will also examine smoke alarm compliance and emergency resources on the island, where fire and rescue crews were nearly an hour away by barge. Hearings are set to run for two weeks.
keyFacts: Fire killed a man and five children in 2023
Inquest opened on Monday
Hearings will run for two weeks

leftOut.title: Bowen presents 18-page COP31 draft calling for faster fossil fuel phase-out
leftOut.summary:
Climate Change Minister Chris Bowen, president of the COP31 negotiations, released an 18-page draft agreement in Antalya, Türkiye, the ABC reported. The draft draws on submissions from 160 countries, calls for accelerated action to phase out fossil fuels and seeks 35 per cent electrification of global energy by 2035.

It also proposes tripling adaptation funding to at least $US120 billion by 2035, according to the ABC. Greenpeace described the language as among the strongest in a COP draft. Bowen said not all parties would agree. Critics pointed to Australia's fossil fuel project approvals; Bowen defended exports to countries in transition.
keyFacts: Draft has 144 provisions
Seeks 35 per cent electrification by 2035
Bowen says the text is not final

leftOut.title: Magnitude 6.6 earthquake near Indonesia's Tanimbar Islands felt across NT Top End
leftOut.summary:
A magnitude 6.6 earthquake struck near Indonesia's Tanimbar Islands at about 6.41am Darwin time on Tuesday, the Bureau of Meteorology said, according to the ABC. Geoscience Australia said it began 42 kilometres beneath the Banda Sea.

More than 450 people reported feeling the tremor across the Northern Territory's Top End, including Darwin, Palmerston and Katherine, the ABC reported. Most shaking was weak or light. The bureau said there was no tsunami threat to Australia, and no damage was reported.
keyFacts: Quake was 42km below the Banda Sea
More than 450 felt reports
No tsunami threat to Australia

leftOut.title: Bureau says possible tornado damaged homes at South West Rocks
leftOut.summary:
The Bureau of Meteorology said it was possible a tornado struck South West Rocks on the NSW Mid North Coast at about 4.45pm on Monday, the ABC reported. The bureau was still assessing radar data and reports.

Three homes lost their roofs, and the SES received more than 30 calls for help, according to the ABC. Elsewhere in north-east NSW, 43 millimetres of rain fell in 30 minutes at Grafton and hailstones up to six centimetres were reported at Lawrence.
keyFacts: Three homes lost roofs
SES received more than 30 calls
Bureau still assessing whether it was a tornado

leftOut.title: Inquest hears Perth teen shot by police consumed extremist material
leftOut.summary:
A forensic psychiatrist told the inquest into the death of 16-year-old James Leslie Hollands that he had consumed extremist online content, including beheading videos, the ABC reported. Hollands was shot dead by police at a Willetton Bunnings in May 2024 after stabbing a man.

Dr Natalie Pyszora said there was no sign he was planning a terror attack and that his risk had been assessed as low, according to the ABC. The family's lawyer questioned police leading the countering violent extremism program, while a senior detective supported it.
keyFacts: Inquest into May 2024 police shooting
Psychiatrist saw no sign of attack planning
Family questions police role in program

leftOut.title: Sam Wood takes bail appeal to Queensland Court of Appeal
leftOut.summary:
Fitness personality Sam Wood, charged with assaulting and strangling his wife on the Sunshine Coast in October, has taken his bail application to the Queensland Court of Appeal, the ABC reported. He intends to contest the allegations.

After two unsuccessful bail applications, his lawyers argued a Supreme Court judge's refusal was unreasonable and did not consider whether proposed conditions would reduce risk, according to the ABC. The court heard allegations about an argument in which he is accused of grabbing his wife by the throat.
keyFacts: Charged over alleged October assault
Two earlier bail bids failed
He intends to contest the charges

leftOut.title: Trump scheduled to sign trade deal with Thailand during Manila visit
leftOut.summary:
Donald Trump was scheduled to sign a trade agreement with Thailand during his visit to Manila for the ASEAN summit, AP reported on Tuesday. Trump has said Thailand will eliminate tariffs on US exports under the deal.

AP did not report details of the agreement or confirm that it had been signed. Trump is in Manila for an ASEAN-US special summit and talks with Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr before travelling to China for the APEC meeting in Shenzhen.
keyFacts: Signing scheduled during Manila visit
Terms not yet published
Trump travels on to APEC in China

leftOut.title: Trump says US has concluded trade deal with Philippines; no details released
leftOut.summary:
Donald Trump said at a state luncheon in Manila that the US had concluded a large trade deal with the Philippines, Reuters reported. He did not give details, and Manila did not announce an agreement.

The office of President Ferdinand Marcos Jr had no immediate comment, according to Reuters. Trump also said Thailand would remove tariffs on US goods under a deal expected in the coming weeks. Marcos said separately that no agreement on the US-led Pax Silica technology initiative would be signed during the visit, The Chronicle reported.
keyFacts: No terms have been published
Philippine officials have not confirmed the deal
Trump travels on to APEC in China

leftOut.title: Trump, Xi and Putin due to hold three-way meeting in China on Thursday
leftOut.summary:
US President Donald Trump is due to hold a three-way meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin in China on Thursday, Al Jazeera reported. The White House and the Kremlin announced the plan last week, according to The Washington Post.

The meeting is set for the sidelines of the APEC summit in Shenzhen. No agenda has been published. The talks were first reported several days ago, and no new details were released on Wednesday.
keyFacts: Meeting due on Thursday
Held on the sidelines of APEC in Shenzhen
Announced by the White House and Kremlin

leftOut.title: Ukrainian community group criticises Albanese over summit photo with Lavrov
leftOut.summary:
Prime Minister Anthony Albanese appeared alongside Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov in the East Asia Summit family photo in Manila on Tuesday, AAP reported. Kateryna Argyrou, who chairs the Australian Federation of Ukrainian Organisations, told AAP the image was deeply disappointing.

Albanese did not rule out appearing in a photo with Vladimir Putin at APEC in China, according to AAP. In his summit address, he condemned Russia's war against Ukraine as unprovoked and unjustified.
keyFacts: The photo was taken at the East Asia Summit in Manila
Lavrov represented Russia at the summit
Albanese condemned the war in his address

leftOut.title: AUSTRAC chief says some Australians turn a blind eye to money laundering
leftOut.summary:
AUSTRAC chief executive Brendan Thomas said in a Sydney speech that some ordinary business people are helping criminals launder money, AAP reported. He said he was concerned by how willing some members of the public were to ignore financial crime.

Thomas said businesses newly covered by anti-money laundering rules since July had filed more than 1,000 reports, according to AAP. He also pointed to illicit tobacco, crypto ATMs, bookkeepers offering laundering services and scam bots built with artificial intelligence.
keyFacts: New rules took effect in July
Newly regulated businesses have filed more than 1,000 reports
Thomas spoke in Sydney on Wednesday

leftOut.title: Microsoft's Nadella urges Australian firms to treat some AI models as insider risks
leftOut.summary:
Microsoft chief executive Satya Nadella told an AI event in Sydney that businesses adopting artificial intelligence should do so with high ambition, but treat some models as an insider risk, AAP reported. He said much more work was needed on AI safety.

Nadella spoke in a pre-recorded conversation with Commonwealth Bank chief executive Matt Comyn. AAP reported the Australian Cyber Security Centre issued more than 4,400 warnings of potential malicious activity last financial year, up 80 per cent. CBA announced a free cybersecurity tool called CodeCheck.
keyFacts: Nadella spoke in a pre-recorded session
Cyber warnings rose 80 per cent last financial year
CBA launched a free tool called CodeCheck

leftOut.title: Undecided voters rate Wilson ahead of Carroll in Victorian leaders' debate
leftOut.summary:
Opposition Leader Jess Wilson was rated best by 39 per cent of 100 undecided voters at Tuesday night's Victorian leaders' debate, AAP reported. Premier Ben Carroll was rated best by 7 per cent, Greens leader Ellen Sandell by 25 per cent and One Nation leader Warren Pickering by 16 per cent.

Wilson and Carroll exchanged remarks about former premiers, according to AAP. A Redbridge survey published in the Australian Financial Review put the Coalition on 31 per cent, Labor 23, One Nation 22 and the Greens 15. Carroll said he was focused on the vote on 28 November.
keyFacts: The audience was 100 undecided voters
Election day is 28 November
Early voting began on Wednesday

leftOut.title: Tasmanian premier signals possible cost rise for Hobart AFL stadium
leftOut.summary:
Tasmanian Premier Jeremy Rockliff told parliament it would be no surprise if costs for the Macquarie Point stadium in Hobart increased, AAP reported. The 23,000-seat roofed stadium was last estimated at $1.13 billion, up from an initial budget of $715 million.

Rockliff did not say whether the government would keep its $875 million funding cap or seek parliament's approval for more money, according to AAP. Greens leader Rosalie Woodruff and independent Meg Webb called for transparency. A cost update is due by 23 November.
keyFacts: Current estimate is $1.13 billion
The federal government is contributing $240 million
A cost update is due by 23 November

leftOut.title: Court releases ballistics videos in murder trial of former NSW police officer
leftOut.summary:
The NSW Supreme Court has released police ballistics reconstruction videos from the murder trial of former senior constable Beau Lamarre-Condon, AAP reported. He has pleaded not guilty to murdering Jesse Baird and Luke Davies in Paddington in February 2024.

The Crown alleges Baird was shot twice and Davies once, according to AAP. Lamarre-Condon says he shot Baird once in self-defence and that the second shot and Davies's death were accidental. Closing submissions are due to begin on Thursday.
keyFacts: The accused has pleaded not guilty
Evidence in the trial closed on Monday
Closing submissions begin Thursday

leftOut.title: Defence calls Crown case weak in trial of former RAAF pilot accused of murder
leftOut.summary:
Defence barrister Saul Holt KC told a Brisbane jury the prosecution case against former RAAF pilot Robert John Crawford was one of the weakest circumstantial cases a court would see, AAP reported. Crawford is accused of killing his wife Frances at their property west of Brisbane in July 2024 and staging a lawnmower accident.

In his closing address, Holt disputed the Crown's description of the couple's marriage and pointed to a late-night text message from Frances, according to AAP. The Crown is due to begin its closing on Thursday.
keyFacts: Crawford is a former RAAF pilot
The alleged death occurred on 30 July 2024
Crown closing begins Thursday
