leftOut.title: Vet practice apologises after Melbourne Cup runner's remains filmed in skip bin
leftOut.summary:
A veterinary practice has apologised after footage showed the body of Melbourne Cup runner So You Are in a skip bin at a waste facility in Sydney, AAP reported. The horse, which finished eighth in the Cup, was euthanised on Monday after colic.

REC Equine Specialists said it did not carry out the burial but had chosen the provider, and had stopped using it, according to AAP. Trainer Bjorn Baker said he was deeply distressed. Racing NSW said it would take action if its investigation found wrongdoing.
keyFacts: The horse ran eighth in the Melbourne Cup
Footage was filmed at Lucas Heights
Racing NSW is investigating

leftOut.title: 40th ARIA Awards held in Sydney with Genesis Owusu and Tame Impala leading nominations
leftOut.summary:
The 40th ARIA Music Awards are being held at Sydney's Hordern Pavilion, AAP reported. Genesis Owusu and Tame Impala lead the nominations with eight each, followed by Ecca Vandal with seven.

Ocean Alley guitarist Mitch Galbraith used the red carpet to criticise proposed federal laws he said would favour AI companies over Australian artists, according to AAP. Wiggles member John Pearce said he agreed. The ceremony is hosted by Melanie Bracewell and Tim McDonald.
keyFacts: This is the 40th ARIA Awards
Two acts lead with eight nominations
Held at the Hordern Pavilion

leftOut.title: England beat Australia by 97 runs in Hobart to win ODI series 2-1
leftOut.summary:
England beat Australia by 97 runs in the third one-day international in Hobart on Wednesday to win the series 2-1, the ABC reported. England had lost the first match in Perth.

Ben Duckett scored 133 from 115 balls as England made 328, according to the ABC. Australia were bowled out for 231 in the 47th over. Cameron Green was struck on the helmet by a bouncer and left the field. Matt Renshaw took three wickets for Australia and Sonny Baker took four for England.
keyFacts: England won by 97 runs
Duckett scored 133
England took the series 2-1

leftOut.title: English press turns on Cummins after Khawaja book revives ball-tampering affair
leftOut.summary:
English newspapers have criticised Australian Test captain Pat Cummins after claims about the 2018 ball-tampering affair in Usman Khawaja's autobiography, the ABC reported. Columnists in the Daily Mail and The Telegraph said his credibility had been damaged.

Cameron Bancroft, one of three players banned over the affair, published a long article in The West Australian claiming the whole team knew about the sandpaper, according to the ABC. Cummins's management says he had no knowledge of the plan. Cricket Australia has announced a forum for players and staff.
keyFacts: The claims stem from Khawaja's autobiography
Bancroft says the team knew
Cummins's management denies he knew

leftOut.title: People with disability call for more accessible music festivals
leftOut.summary:
Music fans with disability say festivals need to do more to include them, the ABC reported ahead of the International Day of People with Disability. A 2022 Creative Australia survey found 40 per cent of people with disability attend festivals, compared with 45 per cent of others.

Rapper MC Wheels said a lack of accessible toilets was a major barrier, according to the ABC. Ability Fest, founded in 2018, was cited as Australia's first inclusive festival. A researcher said exclusion was often created by environments and systems rather than impairment.
keyFacts: 40 per cent of people with disability attend festivals, a survey found
Accessible toilets were named as a key barrier
Ability Fest began in 2018

leftOut.title: ABC analysis says Australia keeps moving closer to US despite Trump's volatility
leftOut.summary:
ABC political editor David Speers wrote that Donald Trump's meeting with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen is awkward for US allies including Australia. He pointed to Australia signing the US-led declaration on AI supply chains and the Quad's agreement in Manila on maritime surveillance and a first joint exercise next year.

Speers argued that Australia is still drawing closer to the United States despite Prime Minister Anthony Albanese's cautious tone towards Trump. He noted Albanese said he would raise concerns about the Iran war with the US President.
keyFacts: The piece is an analysis column
It cites the Quad maritime surveillance plan
It cites Australia's signing of the AI declaration

leftOut.title: ABC previews what Trump, Putin and Xi want from Shenzhen meeting
leftOut.summary:
The ABC's China correspondent previewed the first three-way meeting of Donald Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin, due on the sidelines of APEC in Shenzhen. The White House listed nuclear arms control, the wars in Ukraine and Iran, trade and AI as topics.

Analysts quoted were sceptical of concrete outcomes, and no joint press conference or communique is expected, the ABC reported. The New START treaty lapsed in February. A White House spokeswoman said Trump viewed nuclear proliferation as very dangerous, while a Kremlin aide pointed to the meeting's symbolism.
keyFacts: The meeting is the first of its kind
No joint communique is expected
New START lapsed in February

leftOut.title: About 20 isolated Awá people sighted near village in Brazil's Maranhão
leftOut.summary:
Around 20 isolated Awá people were sighted on Monday in the Arariboia Indigenous territory in Brazil's Maranhão state, according to Brazil's Ministry of Indigenous Peoples, AAP reported. The ministry said the information was preliminary.

Survival International said the group asked a government team for yams and took them back into the forest, according to AAP. It estimates about 100 Awá remain uncontacted. Officials activated an emergency response because of disease risk, and Indigenous affairs agency and health staff are in the area.
keyFacts: About 20 people were sighted
Survival estimates about 100 uncontacted Awá
Officials activated an emergency response

leftOut.title: Von der Leyen presses EU states on €45 billion Ukraine loan for 2027
leftOut.summary:
European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen is seeking support for a €45 billion loan to Ukraine for 2027, backed by joint EU borrowing, Euronews reported. It would be split into €25 billion for military needs and €20 billion for budget support, covering about two-thirds of Kyiv's expected shortfall.

Ukraine would repay only once Russia pays reparations, according to Euronews. The plan needs unanimous backing before next week's EU summit, and Hungary, Slovakia, Czechia and Bulgaria are resisting. The Commission first proposed the loan in late October.
keyFacts: The loan totals €45 billion
€25 billion is for military needs
It needs unanimous support from 27 members

leftOut.title: Crossbench MPs oppose Labor's late changes to electoral funding laws
leftOut.summary:
Special Minister of State Don Farrell tabled late amendments to federal electoral funding laws that take effect on 1 January, AAP and Guardian Australia reported. The government described the changes as technical. The opposition said it would support them.

The amendments would let parties grow investment funds without the interest counting toward donation caps, Guardian Australia reported. Independent MP Kate Chaney called it a major-party stitch-up, and Senator David Pocock said uncapped money could flow to major parties. Farrell said the reforms aim to end a donations arms race. Zoe Daniel and Rex Patrick are challenging the caps in the High Court.
keyFacts: The laws take effect on 1 January 2027
The opposition will support the amendments
A High Court challenge is under way

leftOut.title: Gulf states seek partial deal as concerns grow of renewed US-Iran war
leftOut.summary:
Concerns are growing about a return to full-scale conflict between the US and Iran, AAP reported. At a White House news conference on Friday, President Donald Trump said Iran wanted a deal but not one acceptable to him, and repeated that Iran would never have a nuclear weapon.

An unnamed Middle Eastern diplomat said Gulf Arab states were seeking a partial arrangement that would ease shipping limits in the Strait of Hormuz in exchange for limited sanctions relief for Iran, AAP said. Iran has widened attacks on Gulf neighbours in the past week after a US strike on Qeshm Island. US forces continue a naval blockade of Iranian ports.
keyFacts: Trump said Iran's terms were not acceptable
An unnamed diplomat said Gulf states seek a partial deal
A US naval blockade of Iranian ports continues

leftOut.title: Carroll says Victorian election is winnable as poll shows Labor behind
leftOut.summary:
Victorian Premier Ben Carroll said every election is winnable ahead of the 28 November state poll, AAP reported. Carroll took over five months ago after a leadership spill that led to Jacinta Allan's resignation.

A RedBridge Group and Accent Research survey published in the Australian Financial Review put the Coalition on 31 per cent, Labor on 23 per cent and One Nation on 22 per cent, AAP said. Carroll is defending his seat of Niddrie, which he held in 2022 on a 6.7 per cent margin. He acknowledged Labor faced a difficult contest but said he would keep campaigning across the state.
keyFacts: The election is on 28 November
The RedBridge survey had Labor on 23% primary vote
Carroll is defending Niddrie on a 6.7% margin

leftOut.title: Kensington Palace announces documentary on Princess of Wales's cancer treatment
leftOut.summary:
Kensington Palace has announced a documentary, Heal, about the Princess of Wales's experience of cancer, the ABC reported, citing AFP and Reuters. It will air on the BBC on 29 November and on Channel Nine in Australia on 1 December.

The palace said the film follows her on the Three Peaks Challenge, which she completed in June, and features others facing serious illness. Catherine announced in March 2024 that she was being treated for cancer and said in January 2025 that she was in remission. The palace said funds from distribution will go to the Royal Marsden Cancer Charity.
keyFacts: The documentary airs on the BBC on 29 November
It screens on Channel Nine on 1 December
Proceeds go to the Royal Marsden Cancer Charity

leftOut.title: ABC analysis examines Albanese's diplomacy after APEC and Quad trip
leftOut.summary:
An ABC analysis by chief digital political correspondent Clare Armstrong reviews Prime Minister Anthony Albanese's 11-day trip, which included the Quad meeting in Manila and APEC in China. It notes that Albanese told Russian President Vladimir Putin at APEC to end the war in Ukraine, and that US President Donald Trump met Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping in Shenzhen.

Armstrong argues Albanese has grown more comfortable managing relations with Beijing and Washington but has limited influence over decisions made by the three leaders. The piece is analysis and does not report new events beyond those already covered.
keyFacts: The trip lasted 11 days and included APEC and the Quad
Albanese urged Putin to end the war, the ABC said
The piece is analysis, not new reporting
